title: Feature Updates for CRM 3.11 and Site 4.16
body:
Introduction

*Please note that the features available to you on the Lofty platform will vary depending on the package you have purchased. For any questions related to your package, please contact our Support Team or your assigned Customer Success Manager for more information.

Release Date

All features in this update are scheduled for release on Monday, September 28, 2020.

Summary

  • Lofty Marketplace
  • Improved Zillow Lead Tagging
  • Email Parsing Duplicate Improvement
  • Individual Billing for Enterprise Teams and Individual Agents
  • Pocket Listing Location Coordinates

 

Lofty Marketplace

Lofty now has a new section called "Marketplace." In this location, you will be able to access Lofty add-on services. Upcoming releases will also include third-party apps and services that you can get more information on via the Marketplace.

In the first version of the Marketplace, you will be able to access the following Lofty services. Some of these can be added automatically and others will issue a request for a Lofty rep to coordinate a call to implement as needed.

  • Buyer Lead Gen
  • Seller Lead Gen
  • Direct Mail
  • AI Assistant
  • Power Dialer / Three Line Dialer
  • Text Package
  • Adding Seats
  • Lofty Package Upgrade

 

Improved Zillow Lead Tagging

If integrated correctly (see Zillow Integration), Zillow leads will now have additional information added to their lead profile. Basically, what this means is that Zillow sends additional information to Lofty via API and Lofty will add this information as tags. The following table outlines what is sent from Zillow and what the corresponding tag will be in Lofty:

Additional Info from Zillow
Value
Tag Name in Lofty
IsConnected False NotConnected
IsConnected True Connected
Is Tour False NotTour
Is Tour True Zillow Property Tour
Contact Message The words "Property Tour" are contained in the initial contact message Zillow Property Tour
Contact Message The word "Connected" is contained in the initial contact message Zillow Concierge

The following scenarios apply when the additional info from Zillow is combined:

  • If IsConnected=true and the Contact Message does or does not have the word "Connected," then the system will only add a "Connected" tag
  • If IsConnected=false but the Contact Message has the word "Connected," then the "Zillow Concierge" tag will be added
  • If IsTour=true and the Contact Message does or does not have the word "Property Tour," then the system will only add a "Zillow Property Tour" tag
  • If IsTour=false but the Contact Message has the word "Property Tour," then the system will add a "Zillow Property Tour" tag

"Connected" in Zillow's terms, refers to leads that have left a message and have been connected to you via the Zillow Concierge service. For example, here is a note that is added to Lofty that would contain this information:

"Tour" refers to a lead that has requested a tour via Zillow.

So, what you will want to take a look at the different tags and scenarios and potentially build out a Smart Plan to auto-respond or trigger tasks depending on your workflow. Or, at least, you can use the tags to easily filter your leads in the future or have the necessary background when referencing a lead profile page.

 

Email Parsing Duplicate Improvement

Many leads enter Lofty via email parsing (the new lead email alert is parsed into the Lofty platform automatically). There is currently existing logic in place to handle duplicate leads. The following shows the current logic as well as the improvement that has been made here:

Existing Logic: Lead A and Lead B both have email addresses and they are the same. This would be flagged as a duplicate lead.

Improved Logic: Lead A and Lead B do not have email addresses so the system will check the phone and name (first, last). If the phone and name are the same, the lead will be flagged as a duplicate lead. 

*Note: If a lead does not have email/phone, it will not be imported to Lofty during the email parsing process

More information on duplicate leads can be referenced in the following article: Duplicate Leads + Merging Duplicates. Email parsing details can be found here: Lead Capture/Email Parsing.

 

Individual Billing for Enterprise Teams and Individual Agents

With the improvements made in this release, individual teams under an Enterprise as well as individual agents can pay for their own lead generation campaigns. Individual agents will need to have their own Subdomain/Agent Website in order for this to be possible.

  • Enterprise Team Owners/Admins and individual agents can purchase lead generation directly in the CRM and use their own card to pay for it. If no card is on file, the system can collect that information directly. 
  • This can be accessed via Campaigns > Buyer/Seller Lead Gen
  • Clicking on the button to "See how many leads I can get" will provide an estimated CPL for lead generation campaigns.
  • Immediately following the purchase of Buyer/Seller Lead Gen campaigns, Lofty will prompt you to provide access to your Facebook Business Page which will be used to run the ads. After Lofty receives authorization for Facebook and has coordinated the target audience, etc., the ads can begin without delay.

 

Pocket Listing Location Coordinates

Users with access to the Pocket Listing feature can now add a customized "Location Point" with longitude and latitude coordinates. This will increase the accuracy of the map center point when displayed on the Lofty website.

You can also select a specific point on a map to find the exact coordinates and add to the pocket listing location information. Selecting the point and clicking "OK" results in the specific coordinates being added.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com> or by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557.

name: Lead Import (via Google Contacts)
title: Lead Import (via Google Contacts)
body:
Introduction

Unless you are brand new to the world of real estate, you will likely have people you are already working with before joining Lofty. With that in mind, here is a brief description of how to import leads into the Lofty CRM from Google Contacts.

*IMPORTANT:

  • To learn how to import leads from a spreadsheet/CSV, please take a look at the following article: Lead Import (via CSV/Spreadsheet).
  • This Integration with Google Contacts allows for manually pulling the data from Google Contacts, but is not intended to be a two-way sync. In other words, if you add a person's information on Lofty/Google Contacts, it will not automatically appear on the other platform. If you are interested in exploring a two-way sync, consider using products such as Zapier.
  • It is usually best practice to wait to upload your leads until after your Lofty website is live and working in case you want to send a welcome email (see Set Up the Welcome Email) or set these leads up on auto property alerts (see Setting Up and Using Auto-Property Alerts). Without the website having the MLS data fully integrated, neither of those two options is possible. 
  • If you want to move more than 200 leads at a time from one agent to another, kindly reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your CRM.

 

Steps

There are two entrances in getting to the Lead Import page.
1. People Page> click the + Add Lead then choose Import Lead.

2. Navigate to Settings > Lead Import > From Google Contacts: 

If you have not already done so, you will be prompted to integrate your Google Contacts accounts. 

You will select the account you want to use from Google:

You will need to give Lofty all the necessary permissions:

Now that Google Contacts is integrated, you will want to click on the "Connect your Google Contacts" button again:

You will be prompted to choose "All" or a specific set of labels:


Tip: The label is different from the columns when imported via CSV. You can see in the image below that the label can be understood as the tag or segment of contacts. The label is used to separate different Google contacts, so if you also want to sync the label, choose a segment for a different label.

 




Finally, you will need to choose from all of the options below and then click the blue "Import" button, and then "Confirm" on the last prompt:

Depending on the number of leads, your import should process quickly, and you will have access to your clients in Lofty. 

Remember, any changes on Lofty will not be reflected in Google Contacts, and any changes in Google Contacts will not be reflected in Lofty.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your CRM.

body:
Introduction

*Please note that the features available to you on the Lofty platform will vary depending on the package you have purchased. For any questions related to your package, please contact our Support Team or your assigned Customer Success Manager for more information.

Release Date

All features in this update are scheduled for release on Wednesday, September 2, 2020 with the exception of "Improved Mobile Navigation for Listings" which is scheduled for Friday, September 4, 2020.

Summary 

  • Menu Layout Change
  • New Transaction Detail Page
  • Transaction Checklists
  • Support for Searching Listings by Full Listing Address (Original & New CMS）

  • Form Block Button Action Optimization (New CMS Only)
  • Landing Page Registration Rules Optimization (New CMS Only)

 

Menu Layout Change

A quick change that is worth pointing out is that the layout of the main navigation menu has changed. The available options on the menu have not changed, but their order has been adjusted in order to provide more structured access to the most-used features on the platform.

Previous layout:

 

Updated layout:

 

New Transaction Detail Page

A new Transaction Detail Page has been built as the central location for upcoming Transaction Management improvements. 

The transaction name is displayed directly at the top along with the transaction owner and the associated lead:

The transaction stages at the top are clickable to move the transaction through the transaction pipeline:

You can easily edit, delete, or send to an integrated platform (Brokermint, etc.) using the options at the top-right:

The available tabs in the main section include the following:

  • Checklists. See below. This is a new feature with this release.
  • Accounting. Includes the numbers of the transaction.
  • Vendors/Partners. See How to Assign a Vendor/Partner to a Transaction.
  • History. Displays a log of all changes/actions to this specific transaction.

 

Transaction Checklists

Along with the redesign to the Transaction Detail Page, a new Transaction Checklist feature can be used to create tasks that are triggered at each stage of the transaction. This is done by creating templates that can then be applied to a transaction. These templates can only be edited by the Team Owner/Admin or those on the team who have the "Manage Team" permission (see Team Permissions).

For more information on this new feature, please reference the following Help Center article: Transaction Management Checklists.

 

Support for Searching Listings by Full Listing Address 

*Available on Original & New CMS

An improvement has been made to the buyer searching experience on your Lofty IDX website. Previously, searching for a specific address would not produce viable results. With this release, we have now made it possible to search a specific address without the obstacles that previously existed. If a visitor to your site has a specific address in mind that they want to find, they can easily use the search bar to find it:

 

Improved Mobile Navigation for Listings

*Only available on New CMS

With this release, visitors to the mobile version of your site will be able to more easily navigate between listing detail pages and the original list the were viewing. With the “down” arrow, visitors can go back to the property list (including map view and grid view), and they can use the "PREV" and "NEXT" buttons to go back and forth on the list.

Also, in order to better capture lead information, common actions be leads are presented/pinned to the bottom of the screen:

 

Form Block Button Action Optimization

*Only available on New CMS

Due to restrictions by some browsers (including Safari), an additional configuration has been added to the Form Block (see Form Block) that will confirm the redirect prior to sending the site visitor to another page. Existing forms will have this functionality applied to them.

This is where the new settings are located when editing any form block:

When the "Toast" option is selected, it will not redirect the user and instead will display a pop-up with the wording that you choose:

When the "Destination URL" option is selected, there are a couple more options. You will choose the "Thank You Message" as well as the button description for the redirect option, and then you will select a destination URL. Leaving it with the "/" will send the user to the Home page when clicked.

The new option to "Turn on to Preview the Button Action" will show what the action will look like when the form is submitted. For example:

 

Landing Page Registration Rules Optimization

*Only available on New CMS

Landing page registration settings have been improved to make the transition to a redirected page work more smoothly. With this improvement, the registration rules of the landing pages will take effect on both the landing page and the pages after it redirects. This will allow users to better control the registration pop-up on this transition.

*IMPORTANT: Please note that if you plan to test the registration rules (which is always a good idea), be aware that having the main IDX website and a landing page open at the same time and in the same browsing session, etc. will likely cause a conflict. Be sure to test using a new incognito window each time you test or be sure to clear the browser cache and cookies.

 

Questions?

AI Assistant: "Assigned Agent" Control

In this release, users who have purchased the AI Assistant can control whether or not the AI Assistant will work leads depending on who they are assigned to. If you do not want the AI Assistant to follow up on leads assigned to a specific agent, you can now deselect them on the drop-down list under the AI Assistant settings. This option is available for both NEW incoming leads and EXISTING leads as well:

 

Smart Plan Last Modified Timestamp

A new timestamp has been added under the "Plan Name" of each Smart Plan in both My Smart Plans and Team Smart Plans. The timestamp simply records the last modified date/time. Currently, you cannot sort by the last modified time.

 

Market Snapshot Email

*Only available on the New CMS

As mentioned in the previous release (see Feature Updates for CRM 3.7.0 and Site 4.12: Market Snapshot Page & Block), the Market Snapshot Email will now send any buyer/seller who clicks the blue "See More Details" button to the updated Market Snapshot page where it will populate the data based on the email they were looking at. 

If clients have old market snapshot emails, those links will still go to old market snapshot pages that will display the data in the old format. The pages will not be dead.

 

Multiple Logos

*Only available on the New CMS

When using the CMS Tool to edit your website header, you now have the option to add a second logo. Simply double-click the header block and then scroll down to the "Logo2" section of the settings on the left where you can now add an additional logo. You can also customize the alt text, logo size, and even link when clicked. Note that you can only add one extra logo on the main website (via the Home page settings - Header), but you can add individual logos on any landing pages that are built (see Landing Pages). 

 

Listing Map Optimization for Mobile Devices

*Only available on the New CMS

The map search pattern that displays when browsing your site listings on a mobile device has been optimized. It is now easier to zoom in on the map and the interaction with the map itself is more intuitive. Site visitors can also see where the properties are on the map more clearly. They can find the area they want to look and then click the "Search This Area" button to search that specific zone. Overall, the user interface is now more clear and buyers can find the location they are looking for and access the available tools (draw, schools, satellite view, etc.) more quickly.

name: In-Depth: Round Robin & Next Up

body:
Introduction

This article is an in-depth analysis of the logic behind the round-robin and Next-Up lead distribution methods. Please only reference this article if you want to better understand very specific information about how the routing logic works. For basic information on lead routing, please refer to the following article: Agent Lead Routing Rules.

 

In-Depth Round Robin & Next-Up Logic

Definitions

First of all, there are a few important definitions associated with the Next Up and Round Robin distribution methods:

a. Cycle. A "cycle" lasts until all of the leads that are planned for distribution in a single lead routing rule are assigned to agents. In the screenshot below, for example, you see one cycle consisting of a total of 30 leads being distributed to five different agents. 6+6+6+3+9 = 30. When a cycle ends, the rule will start all over again. 

b. Allocation. This customizable value refers to the total number of leads that is to be assigned to each assignee. The percentage shows how it compares to the other assignees on the list. In the screenshot above, you can see where you can define the allocation for each agent in the assignee list.

c. Hunger. A value associated with each assignee that changes for each one individually if they claim a lead. Hunger starts equal to the allocation (b). The first lead distributed in a rule is always assigned left to right.

But at the second lead and on, the "hunger" of an agent changes for an agent if they claim that lead. Here is the formula that is used to calculate hunger after a lead is claimed:

new hunger = (hunger - 1) ÷ allocation

So, let's look at an example to illustrate all of this in a real-world scenario:

We will look at "Next Up" as the distribution method because this adds a potential outcome that is important to be aware of but doesn't exist in "Round Robin."

Introduction

"Porting" is the process of moving phone numbers between providers. If you want to port an existing number out of Lofty, note that you will need to contact the new carrier to which you’d like to port your numbers (e.g., Verizon, AT&T, etc.). Please note that portability rules vary by carrier, and not all carriers accept this process. But, for carriers where porting is an option, the process generally works as described here:

  1. Most carriers require you to fill out a Letter of Authorization, or LOA.
  2. You will typically be asked to provide specific information as proof of your ownership of the number. You can contact your Customer Success Manager (CSM) or the Lofty Support Team (support@lofty.com) to request this information. 
  3. If everything you submit is sufficient information, your request will then be submitted to our carrier partner as a port request. If, for some reason, your port-out request is rejected by the receiving provider, please contact us at Lofty and let us know what number(s) you are trying to port out and the specific denial reason(s) provided to you by your new carrier that resulted in rejection.
  4. Once Lofty receives the port away notification from the provider, we will email you to confirm your request. After you confirm this request is valid, our carrier partner will schedule the port date with your new carrier.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Port In Number(s) to Lofty
title: Port In Number(s) to Lofty
body:
Introduction

"Porting" is the process of moving phone numbers between providers.

Porting is a multi-step process that takes an average of four weeks if there are no blockers. Common blockers include: inaccurate PIN numbers, account name mismatch, incorrect billing address, etc. This four-week timeline is an estimate and will likely vary from case to case. The process includes coordination between Lofty's upstream provider and your service provider to transfer the number to Lofty. The four-week estimate could vary because of the need to interact with a variety of parties during this process.

 

*IMPORTANT:

  • Lofty only supports porting in U.S. and Canadian local numbers from other providers. Other countries are not currently supported.
  • 10DLC registration must be complete and verified before users are able to text in Lofty. For more information, please see: A2P 10DLC Registration

 

Summary

  • (1) Submit your Porting Request
  • (2) Number is Submitted to Carrier Partner
  • (3) Response from Carrier
  • (4) Porting Date is Scheduled
  • FAQs

 

(1) Submit your Porting Request

Please read the requirements very carefully before submitting your porting request. Porting phone numbers is a timely process and requires all information before submitting. Any incorrect information, such as a mismatched billing phone number or incorrect PIN, will cause a delay in the porting timeline. 

You will need to provide the following when you submit your request:

Notes:

*We recommend that you create a CSV sheet that shows the numbers to be ported, the PIN, and the person that phone number should be assigned to. For example:

 

Once you have gathered all of the required information, you can submit your port request to support@lofty.com or to your Customer Success Manager. 

 

To ensure that your port request processes as smoothly as possible, you will need to make sure all the information provided matches the service information on file with the current carrier. If the information you provide to us does not match the current carrier's records, your port request will be rejected, which will delay the port request until the information you provide matches the information the carrier has on file. If you are not sure about this information, you can contact your current phone service provider.

 

(2) Number is Submitted to the Carrier Partner

If everything in Step 1 was done correctly, your request will then be submitted to your soon-to-be former carrier as a port request. During this time, do not close your account with your carrier and keep your numbers active.

NOTE: Timeframe may be longer depending on the carrier partner.

 

(3) Response from Carrier

At this point, your request will either be approved or rejected:

Approved

If approved, then you will receive a porting date for when your number will be ported to Lofty.

Rejected

This occurs for a variety of reasons, such as an incorrect PIN for an account, an address or zip code that doesn’t match the current carrier’s records or a port request made by an unauthorized user on the account. Additionally, you will need to reach out to your carrier to find out what is needed in order to move forward. Depending on the needs of the carrier, this will add amount of time to your porting request. Step 2 will then be repeated.

 

(4) Porting Date is Scheduled

The Lofty Support Team or your CSM will reach out to you to keep you up-to-date on when your number will be transferred to Lofty. Once you have verified that the number has been transferred to your Lofty project, you can begin using your virtual number on Lofty.

 

 

FAQ

Is there a possibility that the number that is being ported over will be inaccessible/down/offline during the transition process?

The overall process will take up to four weeks to complete, meaning that we need to request our provider to get the number for us. Once they have accepted the ported number, we will change your virtual number to the ported one immediately. This transition should be a seamless one. 

Typically, when a number is moved, there is a scheduled porting date. During that date, there is potential for some downtime. 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

body:
Introduction

Release Date

    • Resume System-Paused Smart Plans

    • Facebook Lead Form Integration: Import Info to Search Criteria

    • Form Block Auto-Tagging 
    • Market Snapshot Page & Block

 

Dashboard Announcement Board

A new section will now be available on the Lofty Dashboard when you first log into Lofty each day. The new section appears directly below the "Today's Hot Listings" section on the Dashboard. For more information on how this new feature can be used, see Dashboard Announcement Board.

 

Microsoft Teams Incoming Webhook Connection

+

If you have a Microsoft Teams account, you can set up some initial connections by adding webhooks in Lofty. The webhooks need to be set up in Microsoft Teams first and then connected to Lofty. 

To learn how to set up Microsoft Teams using Incoming Webhooks, please reference the following article: Microsoft Teams Incoming Webhook Connection. 

Currently, the webhook integration supports the following actions:

  • Share a Lead to Microsoft Teams
  • Share an Announcement to Microsoft Teams

 

Resume System-Paused Smart Plans

With the release of this new feature, the Team Owner/Admin (no one else on the team) can now restart multiple Smart Plans that were paused by the system for a variety of reason in the last 30 days. More information on this feature is outlined in the following section: If the system has auto-paused Smart Plans, is there a way to restart them?.

 

Add to Group Option When Removing an Agent

As the Team Owner/Admin, you are the one responsible for adding/removing agent users from your team. When an agent is removed, this new feature allows for the leads who belong to that agent to be added to a specific GROUP in Lofty so that they can be easily located, redistributed, etc. The group must have already been created in order for it to populate on the list when removing the agent.

You will see this option appear when you go to remove an agent from your team:

 

Facebook Lead Form Integration: Import Info to Search Criteria

The Facebook Lead Form Integration now supports sending additional information from the Facebook Form to Lofty. When you create a lead form on Facebook, it might be built around a specific listing or market area and it would be a good idea to bring that information into Lofty to apply towards lead routing, auto property alerts, etc. 

For more information on how to set this up, please reference the following: How do I add search criteria using the Facebook lead form?

Also, for your information, we have included an additional section that is related to the Facebook Lead Form Integration: How do I set it up so that leads that register on Facebook lead forms do not have to sign up on my site after being sent there?.

 

Multiple Small Smart Plan Optimizations

(1) You can now start creating a new Smart Plan by double-clicking the "Standard Plan" option under Settings > Features > Smart Plans:

(2) When changing between task types (Auto Email, Auto Text, Call, etc.) in a Smart Plan, the system will now remember the content for each type if it was already added. Prior to this, the content would be lost when the task type was changed. Now, you can go back if you added something but wanted to see what another task type looked like.

(3) The default trigger time for the first step is "Immediately," but now the default trigger time for the next steps that are added will be "Wait 1 day(s)":

 

Form Block Auto-Tagging 

*Only available on the New CMS

The Form Block (see Form Block) now has a new setting for adding tags to any leads who register via that form. This can be used to easily find the right leads post-registration on the People page but it is also extremely useful when triggering very specific Smart Plans (see Smart Plans). All existing tags will be populated (see Lead Organization with Tags), but a new tag can also be added here as well. 

Here is what that new feature looks like when editing a form block on the website using the New CMS:

When a tag is added, it will be available on a lead profile. Here is a sample tag called "form tag":

Note that this feature also works for existing leads. If an existing lead fills out the form on the website that has been edited to include tags, those tags will be added to the existing lead's profile.

 

Market Snapshot Page & Block

*Only available on the New CMS

A new "Market Snapshot" page and block template is now available to use on the New CMS. You can use this page/block to show local market trends and all related (sold) listings. In addition, site visitors can change the search criteria depending on what they are looking for which is a valuable way for them to compare local market results from different areas. This is especially useful for seller leads.

For more information on how the page and block can be set up and used, please reference the following articles:

  • Market Snapshot Page
  • Market Snapshot Block

Along with this change, note that the "Market Snapshot" emails will be optimized in an upcoming release so that leads that receive these emails will be redirected to these pages when clicking on links. Currently, the Market Snapshot emails that are sent out (see Property Alerts & Market Snapshots (Lead Engagement)) will have links that, when clicked, will go to the old Market Snapshot pages that are only accessible via the emails.

Facebook Integration Optimization

The process to connect your Facebook Ads to the Lofty CRM has now been optimized to more clearly outline the steps and to confirm that the appropriate access has been given to Lofty in order to receive the leads. A series of steps will now guide you through the process and system checks are in place to monitor the connection to confirm it is working. 

Additional instructions are also given on how to connect additional fields and their data into Lofty.

To learn more about setting up the integration, please reference the following: Facebook Lead Form Ads + Lofty Integration.

 

Search Bar Location Logic Optimization

*Only available on the New CMS

Lofty has optimized our Search Bar to force the site visitors to choose from the provided suggestions in order to better narrow down their searches. This means that if a site visitor simply presses "Enter" on the keyboard or clicks the "Search" icon on the website, it will use the first suggestion as the default input value. When combined with the additional setting to determine what displays at the top (see below), this will increase the accuracy of listings shown when searching.

There are two ways to search listings via the Search Bar.

  1. Exact Search. If you choose one of the provided suggestions from the drop-down menu, the search will show listings based on the category chosen (city, zip code, etc.).
  2. Fuzzy Search. If you type in a value and press the “Enter” button on the keyboard or click the "Search" icon, listings will be shown without category restrictions (city, zip code, etc.). 

With this update, there is now an option to switch between the two options in the new CMS Tool > Settings > Listings > Location Search Bar: 

 

Search Bar Location Type Options

*Only available on the New CMS

With this update, there is a new setting to customize what categories (city, neighborhood, zip code) appear when a site visitor uses the search bar on your Lofty IDX website. 

The new setting is located under CMS Tool > Settings > Listings > Location Search Bar. With these settings you can do the following:

  • Hide/Display
  • Reorder (determines which one displays first, second, etc.)
  • Rename

Lead Import Reversal Timeframe Extension

body:
Introduction

Lofty users can collaborate on leads in a variety of ways using the Lofty platform, even across Groups on an Enterprise account. This article will describe all of those options. 

 

Summary

  • Lead Access
  • Collaborating / Sharing Notes
  • Tasks
  • Document Sharing
  • Lender Collaboration

Lead Access

If you want certain people to have access to leads within your account, you can manage their visibility via lead privacy and user permissions. 

  • Lead Privacy: Team Leads vs. Personal Leads
  • Team Permissions

In summary, as long as a user has access to a lead, collaboration can happen between those users within the lead profile.

 

Collaborating / Sharing Notes

By design, all notes and logs will be shared with anyone who has access to a lead. When a note is made, all individuals in the "Assigned To" section (and those with admin access) will have access to view that note. No notifications will be sent to those individuals by default, however. Instead, in order to send a notification to another user with access to that lead, users can @tag each other in notes to send notifications to the other party by doing the following within a lead profile for a specific lead. . .

This is what the sender would see when doing the @tag:

When the @tag is used, a push notification will be triggered via the app/web as well as via email to the person tagged. This is the ideal way to communicate between participating parties.

On the receiving end, this is what the web app notifications will look like:

   

 

The email notification looks like this and includes a link to the lead profile as well as a copy of the note:

The mobile app notifications look like this:

 

Tasks

Tasks can be assigned to anyone who has access to that lead. 

The assignee will then receive a notification that a task is assigned to them. There is no email notification for tasks, but there is a web app and mobile app notification.

Here is what the web app notification for a task assignment looks like: 

Here is what the mobile app notification looks like:

 

Document Sharing

Any documents added to a lead profile will be accessible to any user who has access to that lead.

 

Lender Collaboration

For more information on how to collaborate between agents and lenders, see the following article: Lender and Agent Lead Collaboration.

 

Lead Referrals

You can share a lead with any other agent, even if they are not on the same Lofty account as you. Leads can be shared via email or text, or via the chat feature in the mobile app.

Note: You can only share a lead if you are that lead's primary assigned agent or if you have the Access All Team/Company Lead permission enabled on your Lofty account.

 

Invite via Email

Enter the email address of the agent you would like to share the lead with. They must click "Accept Lead" on the invitation email to view the lead detail page. They will need to log into or create a Lofty account to access the lead's information.

 

Share via Chat

This invite method is only available on the Mobile App. Clicking on the lead card will open the lead detail page.

name: Activities Timeline
title: Activities Timeline
body:
Introduction

 The "Activities Timeline" is a page that provides a good overview of activity happening on your website, with your emails, etc. You can access this landing page by going to Reporting> Marketing> Activities.

Permissions & Lead Privacy

The information seen on this page will depend on the permission level of the user as well as lead privacy settings. If a user has the "Access All Team Leads" permission (see Permissions), the activities shown will be for leads associated with all team members. Also, if a lead is added as a Private Lead, the activity will not be shown on this page unless the user is the owner of that lead (and therefore has access to it (see Lead Privacy: Team Leads vs. Private Leads).

*Currently, there is no way for the Team Admin/Owner (or those with the "Access All Team Leads" permission) to only see activity for their own leads on this page. 

 

Activities Timeline

Use the "Filter By" section at the top to select a timeframe from the following options:

  • This Week
  • This Month
  • This Year
  • All Time

You can also filter the activity type by selecting the type that you would like to see (you can only select one at a time):

  • All Activities
  • Viewed
  • Saved
  • Searched
  • Opened Emails
  • Sell
  • Others

A section right in the middle will point out "Today's Reporting" which includes the number of homes viewed and emails opened.

On the right side, you will see a section for "Active Leads." You can choose to look at the active leads for the following timeframes:

  • This week
  • Last two weeks
  • This month

Clicking on the lead's name in this section or anywhere else on this page will take you to their lead profile. In the "Active Leads" section, you can click on the "eyeball," "heart," or "email" icons to look at the properties they have viewed or favorited or emails they have opened. If they have viewed a property multiple times, that will also be listed here.

The main timeline section will show you the activity as it happens. You are able to see the lead's name as well as any home evaluation requests, searches performed, showings requested, properties viewed, emails opened, etc., all of which are clickable for more in-depth information. Clicking on the lead's name will take you to their lead profile and clicking on an address, search, or evaluation will take you to your website so you can see exactly what they were looking at.

 

Connection to Lead Profile Page

It is worth mentioning that the data populated in the "Activities Timeline" is a summary of the entire database. However, if you simply want to see the activity for a specific person, you can navigate to their lead profile and filter by the activity there. See the Lead Profile Page for more information.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Lender Lead Routing Rules

body:
Introduction

For a detailed explanation of how lead routing works, please reference the following article, as everything in that article applies here as well: Lead Routing Rules.

This article will explore a little more about how lead routing works specifically for lender-type accounts on Lofty. As a review, the lender-type account is different from a standard Lofty agent account. Please reference Being a Lender with Lofty for more information.

 

Summary

  • Lead Routing to Lender
  • Manually-Added Leads & Lender Lead Routing
  • Lofty Paid Leads + Lender Lead Routing

 

Lead Routing to Lender

Lofty can lead routes to any of the different roles available on a lead, including Agent, Assistant, Custom Role, and Lender. The lender slot is always at the bottom of the list, as seen here:

A lender must be an actual lender-type account to be selected in this slot (meaning they cannot be on a standard agent seat). An agent on a team can select a lender from this drop-down in the "Assigned To" section, and this will automatically assign the lead to the lender.

Otherwise, lead routing rules based on source and other criteria can be set up (see Agent Lead Routing Rules for specifics) to route to different lenders, etc. To set this type of rule up, go to Settings > Lead Routing > For Lender:

 

A "Default Rule" can also be set up to assign to no lender, a specific lender, to randomly distribute via Next Up or user Blast Alert as well. All of these distribution methods are described in detail in the referenced article for Agent Lead Routing Rules.

The Lender also has the New Leads button, which allows the Lender to route leads based on the source. 

Manually-Added Leads & Lender Lead Routing

It is important to note that one difference from the Agent Lead Routing Rules is that leads that are manually added via the People page in Lofty are also sent to lenders (though they are not routed to agents, etc.). This means that when a lead is manually added using the option shown in the screenshot above, it will be sent through the "For Lender" rules (if established). If the default rule in that section is "No lender," then none will be assigned.

 

Lofty Paid Leads + Lender Lead Routing

If a lender is set up on a cost-sharing relationship with the agent, specifically for lead generation purposes, they will automatically have the leads assigned to them without having to set up lead routing rules manually. See How to Invite a Lender for more information and note that the lender must be sharing buyer/seller lead generation in order for the automatic assignment to happen.

name: Calling Leads Best Practices
title: Calling Leads Best Practices
body:
Introduction

Calling your leads regularly will help you stay connected to your potential clients--especially if your local market is competitive. Assuming that your competition is also using email drip campaigns, property alerts, market reports, etc., then one of the best ways to stand out is to make sure you have a plan and a tool that you can use to call your leads on a regular basis to stay in contact and build relationships. 

 

Summary

  • Deciding Who To Call
  • Deciding When To Call
  • Suggested Call Frequency
  • Call Script Preparation

Deciding Who To Call

Cold Calling / Prospecting Calling

If you have lead lists like FSBO or expired leads, make sure to import them into Lofty and then organize them by segments/tags (see Lead Organization with Segments or Lead Organization with Tags). You can use Smart Call Lists or Standard Call Lists to call these leads on a regular basis. Lofty also has a Three Line Dialer that you can use to increase your calling efficiency! Click here to add the Three Line Dialer now or click here to upgrade your existing dialer seat.

Standard Call List functionality can be set up using Pipeline stages or Segments. For example, if you imported all FSBO/Expired Leads into Lofty and put them into the "New Leads" pipeline with the tag/segment of "FSBO" or "' Expired," then you can set up two standard call lists: one for Expired Leads and one for FSBO. Remember to give an exact name to the call list so that you can identify it easily.

Example of Segments: 

Example of adding call lists based on Segments: 

After creating these two call lists, you can start dialing by clicking the green call button. 

When cold calling, you will likely come upon leads who ask you to never call them again. For these leads, remember to put them into a "DNC" (Do Not Contact) segment or pipeline stage while you are on the phone with them. This is easy to do because the lead profile will be populated on the left of the screen while you are calling each lead. You may also want to select their number and mark it as DNC as well (if applicable). 

Alternatively, some of your leads may show high interest as buyers or sellers. Just remember to make any notes and move them into the applicable pipeline stage so that you can follow up with them appropriately. Remove them from the segment/pipeline stage that they were in when you started the cold calling to avoid calling them again with the same strategy. 

Smart Call Lists are based on your Lofty tasks that are scheduled for today or are overdue. So, in order for these lists to be populated, you need to make sure you have tasks associated with leads either by adding them manually or by having a Smart Plan assigned that is doing this for you. 

Using Expired Leads as an example, you could prepare a Smart Plan specifically for this type of lead (or consider using some of the built-in plans available in the library). More information on setting up a Smart Plan can be found here: Smart Plans. If you want to do this quickly and easily, you could simply make the Smart Plan 1-3 call tasks. Make sure the tasks are indeed CALL tasks, otherwise, they will not trigger onto the Smart Call lists. 

Be sure to also set up the triggering criteria so that the Smart Plan is auto-applied (if desired) or that you know how to manually apply it later on.

After tasks are associated with leads and due either today or are overdue, these leads will be added automatically to the Smart Call Lists that you can access regularly:

 

Nurturing Leads

If you have a "Nurturing" or a "Cold" pipeline stage in Lofty, you can use those criteria, plus other filters, to set up call lists as previously outlined in this and other linked articles. Reaching out to this type of lead is an important way to stay in contact. A powerful way of using Smart Plans is to mix in manual call tasks with automated emails/texts so that you can call now and again to stay top of mind. 

 

Past Clients

Staying in touch with your past clients will help you get more referrals. With the same logic already explained, consider having a "Past Clients" pipeline stage so that you can call them regularly. Or, combine it with a Smart Plan to send out periodic emails and then trigger a task for you to call as well. Spending time calling past clients is a good investment of your time as long as it is timed correctly. 

 

Deciding When To Call

One Inman Study suggests that calling between 10:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m. yields the best results as far as connection rate is concerned. However, this depends on your area, your client preferences, and the specific individual you are calling. If you can, document the best times to call leads. Categorize your leads so that you know how to handle future calls and can easily access notes to remember any important details before making a phone call.  In the end, find what works best for you and your clients.

 

Suggested Call Frequency

The answer to how many calls you should make in one day depends on your goals and who you are calling. One Inman study explained that it took 208 calls to get an appointment or referral. In other words, it could take about six hours to obtain one appointment. Set your goals for calling based on these basics. Also, keep in mind that you want to tailor your calls to your audience. Do not call leads that you already have a relationship with using the same strategy used for cold calling, etc.

With the Lofty Three Line Dialer, you can easily call through long lists of leads in much less time than you would when dialing out with just one line. Click here to add a new Three Line Dialer package or click here to upgrade your existing dialer package (*IMPORTANT: Only the Team Admin/Owner can buy or upgrade dialer seats)... (Only the team owners can buy or upgrade the dialer). 

 

Call Script Preparation

You do not want to use a script if you are unable to make it sound natural. The key to not sounding robotic is practice, as you already know. Memorize the basics of the script and then practice until it sounds natural. You can always role-play with another agent, your spouse, children, etc.

Do not be afraid to change a script to make it more in tune with your personality and with how the lead responds.

Click here for just one source of cold-calling scripts that you may refer to. You can always search online for more scripts that you might find useful. 

 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

 

Related terms: Lofty dialer, Call and text feature

name: Lead Routing FAQs
title: Lead Routing FAQs
body:
Introduction

This article is to review some of the common questions/concerns related to lead routing within Lofty.
For a detailed explanation of how the lead routing works, please review the following: Lead Routing Rules

 

Summary

  • #1: Why would a lead not go through lead routing?
  • #2: When using Round Robin as the assignment method with the percentage divided equally for all agents, why is the distribution uneven? 
  • #3: Why was a lead distributed to certain people instead of others?
  • #4: As an individual agent/user on the team (not an admin), why was the lead not assigned to me?
  • #5: Is there a way to PAUSE lead routing at night and then have it RESUME again in the morning?
  • #6: Is there a way to trigger lead routing again after a lead has already entered the CRM?
  • #7: Is it possible to have an agent assigned to a lead as one of the "Custom Roles" based on who the assigned agent is? 

 

Questions and Answers

#1: Why would a lead not go through lead routing?

There are four different reasons why a lead will not go through lead routing:

(a) Personal leads will not go through lead routing. Reference Lead Privacy: Team Leads vs. Private Leads for more information on the difference. Only Team Leads are sent through lead routing.

(b) Leads that are added manually will not go through lead routing. If you are adding a lead via this option in Lofty, it will not be sent through lead routing:

(c) If one of the toggle buttons in the lead routing settings is not turned on, new leads that fall into that category will not be sent through lead routing. Note: The routing log (see Lead Routing Logs) will show "N: option unmatched" in this scenario.

(d) The "Assigned to the listing agent" switch is turned on. When the button is ON, if a new lead enters Lofty from a listing on the team IDX website, the lead will automatically be assigned to the listing agent for that specific listing.

 

#2: When using Round Robin as the assignment method with the percentage divided equally for all agents, why is the distribution uneven? 

Please check the working hours of the agent on your team. If the lead was supposed to be assigned to an agent who was not within their working hours, they would be skipped on the distribution list. You can also reference Working Hours & Vacation Mode for more information.

Please also be sure to have the individual agents check their time zone. The time is calculated by the working hours that are tied to the agent's time zone preferences. Differences between agents in their time zone settings could result in an uneven distribution of leads. The time zone is edited here:

 

#3: Why was a lead distributed to certain people instead of others?

There are three possible reasons for this:

  • (a) If the lead routing rule is "Round Robin," check working hours as mentioned in question #2. When the lead is assigned to the agent, if the agent is not in their working hours, it will skip them and assign the lead to the next person in line.
  • (b) If the lead routing method selected is "Next Up" or "Blast Alert," the agent who claims the lead is the one who gets the lead.
  • (c) If both of the previous items are checked, take a look at the timeline for the lead. It might be that during the routing process a user with access to the lead manually assigned the lead, interrupting the lead routing.

You can also refer to this feature for additional information: Lead Routing Logs.

 

#4: As an individual agent/user on the team (not an admin), why was the lead not assigned to me?

In addition to the above possibilities outlined in #1-#3, it might be that the Team Admin/Owner did not add you to the lead routing rules as this is not an automatic process and must be done manually. Check with your Team Admin/Owner to have them make sure you are included in any distribution rules that should apply to you.

 

#5: Is there a way to PAUSE lead routing at night and then have it RESUME again in the morning?

No, currently there is no feature to pause lead routing during a specific schedule. As workarounds, we would recommend setting up your lead routing rules so that Next Up/Blast Alert rules (which require a lead to be claimed) are in place but then a catch-all Round Robin rule with the same assignees that does not require a lead to be claimed. Using this method, if a lead comes in during the middle of the night, it will trigger the Next Up/Blast Alert, but if an agent is not available to claim it, you can still distribute the lead without requiring it to be claimed by using Round Robin. 

Keep in mind that you want to assign the lead to an agent as soon as possible because the Welcome Email (see Set Up the Welcome Email) will not be sent until the assignment is final so it could deter the lead from accessing your site depending on the lead source.

 

#6: Is there a way to trigger lead routing again after a lead has already entered the CRM?

Yes. See Re-Routing Groups.

 

#7: Is it possible to have an agent assigned to a lead as one of the "Custom Roles" based on who the assigned agent is? 

There is no way to just group two users together (for example a lead is assigned to User1 and you always want it to be assigned to User2 in the Assistant slot). This question is typically asked in the context of a husband/wife team, etc. This is not currently possible with lead routing.

What you can do, however, is create rules that are the exact same as those that assign a lead to the agent (For Agent) under each of the custom roles (For #custom_role#). For example, you can grab a source "Zillow," for example, and make sure it always goes to the same agent in the primary "Agent" slot. You could then copy then go to the lead routing rules for the "Assistant" or "Custom Role _____" and assign source "Zillow" to a specific person. That is not going to work for more complicated lead routing where you have multiple assignees for the primary Agent Slot, etc. 

 

More Information

As a reminder, a full outline of how lead routing works in Lofty can be found in the following article should you need to understand more about how lead routing works: Lead Routing Rules.

 

Questions?

name: Introduction to Closely Mobile App
title: Introduction to Closely Mobile App
body:
Introduction

Lofty has released a mobile app that is intended for use by your buyer/seller leads. 

Please keep in mind that this app is not fully supported for every MLS, and we cannot guarantee the listing data. Though we are working to gain MLS approval to use the data, some MLSs might not make their data available, or they might charge a specific amount for using their data on a mobile app that you, as the user, would be responsible for.

Lofty websites, are always a mobile-friendly option that can be used by leads, should Closely not be available.

*IMPORTANT NOTES

You will not be able to sign in on Closely unless (a) you have gotten approval for your account via your MLS and this has been set up by Lofty and (b) you have a test lead that you are signing in as (remember, this is a mobile app for leads, not for you as Lofty users). 

Summary

  • Video Tour
  • Explore Page
    • Search Bar
    • Tools
      • Mortgage
      • Your Agent
      • Featured
      • Valuation
    • My Home
    • Listings
  • Search Page
  • My Home
  • Chat
  • Profile
  • My Tours
  • Closely App Informational Guide
  • FAQs

Video Tour

Explore Page

Upon logging in to the Closely app, the lead will see several options relating to their home buying or selling journey.

Search Bar

At the top of the screen is a search bar. Here, you are able to search for a property by location. Multiple locations may be added, to refine the search:

Tools

Under the search bar is a series of tools:

Mortgage

A mortgage calculator is built into the Closely app, which can help determine the price range for a home purchase.

Your Agent

This section contains the user's real estate agent's contact information, so they may be in touch quickly and easily.

Featured

This tool filters properties per the user's search criteria.

Valuation

This page connects to the Home Valuation page on the Lofty website and allows the users to enter their address to get an update value for their home.

 

My Home

In this section, homeowners can provide their home address and see the current value as well as request to sell the property.

Once the address has been provided, if the MLS has sufficient data to provide a home valuation, it will be available here. There will also be an option to request a Home Report from your Real Estate Agent. If the MLS does not have sufficient data to provide a home value, your Real Estate Agent will be notified to contact you with more information.

Listings

The final section on the Explore Page is MLS listings, filtered by the following categories:

  • Open House: These are listings that have a scheduled open house
  • New: These are listings that are newly on the MLS
  • Price Reduced: Listings that have had a price reduction
  • Recommended: Listings that are recommended for you, per your search criteria

Search Page

The search page allows you to search current homes for sale via a list or map view. Searches may be saved so that you do not have to enter your required filters each time you search for a property.

My Home

This page allows you to track the value of the home you currently own, as well as request to sell the property with your Real Estate Agent.

Chat

The Closely app allows you to chat directly with your Real Estate Agent. Here, you can reach out to your agent quickly and see your previous conversations.

Profile

The profile is your Closely app account information. Here you can see your saved listings and searches, your agent's information, and edit your profile. 

Click the hamburger icon in the upper right corner to enable or disable app notifications, submit Closely app feedback, or log out of the app.

My Tours

Closely app users access their Showings via their profile. Once in the app profile, click My Tours

Tours Tab

This tab allows the user to view the showing appointments and buyer tours that have been confirmed by their agent. The status of the showing will be displayed in the top right corner of each card.

Clicking on a card will take users to the tour detail page, to see more information, like the listing details, time, location, etc. If the tour has been completed, the lead can leave feedback directly in the Closely app.

Requests Tab

This tab shows the record of the user's "Request a Tour" requests from the listing details page. Clicking on the request card will take you to the listing detail page.

Tour Detail Page

The tour detail page is accessed by clicking on a tour in the Tours tab.

The details include:

  1. The entire route for the showing
  2. The scheduled time
  3. The listing information
  4. The driving distance
  5. The driving time.

Users can switch the listing information by clicking on the listing point on the map or sliding the card. Clicking "Directions" will open the map app on users' devices for navigation. If they have not downloaded a map app on their phone, it will prompt them to download one from the app store. Clicking on the "Calendar" icon in the top right corner allows users to add this showing event to their device's calendar.

Listing Feedback

When the showing/tour status is "Completed" the user has the option to leave feedback. The feedback content is the same as the web version.

Push Notifications

The Closely app will send push notifications to users for various events related to a showing, including:

  1. Showing/Tour Creation
  2. Showing/Tour modifications
  3. Showing/tour cancellations
  4. Reminders before the showing starts

Closely App Informational Guide

We have created a guide that may be shared with your leads to teach them about the Closely app and how useful it can be in their home-buying or selling process.

Click here to download the guide

 

FAQs

Q: What services does this app provide to your leads?

A: The app allows buyers/sellers to work closely with his/her home team. All your buyer and seller leads can browse your listings and easily chat online with their agent anytime, anywhere.

---

Q: What can this app bring to you?

A: The app allows you, as an agent, to work closely with your leads. Your leads can receive your messages anytime, anywhere. All lead behavior on the app will be sent to your Lofty CRM as a note on the timeline.

---

Q: How does a lead download this app?

A: You can search for “Closely” on your iPhone or Android device app stores to download directly to your device. The download link could be provided to current leads so that they can sign in and use the features provided.

iPhone Link: Click Here.

Android Link: Click Here.

---

Q: How will your leads use this app?

A: Your leads will use the accounts that they already have registered with your IDX website to log in and browse the available listings populated from the MLS. They can also favorite listings that they can access quickly and easily, and send these listings directly to their assigned agent in Lofty.

---

Q: What if a lead's information (email address) is in the database of more than one Lofty user?

A: If you send the lead your Closely app link, their app will automatically be linked to you. If they download the app on their own, they will have to select who they want to work with. 

---

Q: With the Closely app, can agents pre-load searches, etc.?

A: In Closely, the "Suggested Properties" section in the Buyer Market shows properties from the buyer property alerts set up for that lead by the Lofty user (agent). The "Suggested Properties" section in the Seller Market shows properties from the market snapshot/seller alerts that are set up by the agent.

---

Q: What kind of push notifications are supported for leads via the Closely mobile app?

A: Text or chat messages are supported (though these would also go to the lead's cell number), as well as notifications for new properties that match their criteria and scheduled showings.

---

Q: Closely has an option for leads to send listings to their agent. Who will the message go to in Lofty?

A: The message will be received by the agent in the "Assigned To" section of a lead profile.

---

Q: Can I turn off the Closely app link in my property alert emails?

A: Yes, you can go to your CMS tool Settings> Lead Capture > Closely App. There is a one-day cache for this switch, once you turn it off, it will be removed the next day.

 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

Related terms: Closely app, closely mobile

title: Blank Page
body:
Introduction

Adding a Blank Page

Click on "+ Add Page" at the bottom of the left menu:

Click on the "Blank" template from the available options and then click on "Next":

Adjust the page settings (see Add / Edit Website Pages) and then click on "Save":

A new page is available to edit:

Instructions on how to add/adjust content on a page can be found in the following article: Add / Remove / Edit Blocks on Pages.

 

 

Questions?

name: Property Alerts & Market Snapshots from Mobile App
title: Property Alerts & Market Snapshots from Mobile App
body:
Introduction

After many client requests, the Lofty Mobile App will allow Lofty users to add/edit/delete Property Alerts (buyer) and Market Snapshots via their mobile phones. The filters available on the mobile app will be synced with the web app, meaning if users have specific filters from their MLS set up on the Lofty website, they will also be available on the mobile app. 

Current Limitations include the following: 

  1. Currently, the mobile app does not support the option to "plot" an area on a map when using the mobile app
  2. The ability to send individual listings is not currently supported--only the creation of an alert using the available criteria. This can be done on the desktop web app using Listing Discovery, but is not currently available on the mobile Lofty app. 
  3. Market Reports cannot be created with this feature, only Property Alerts (buyer) and Market Snapshots (seller).

  

 

Questions?
