name: Blog Page
title: Blog Page
body:
Introduction

Adding blog content to your Lofty IDX website is a great way to share valuable content to your site visitors/community/social network and improve the SEO value of your website (see HERE). Creating blog content will be your responsibility (or you can explore third-party services) but you can use the available tools on Lofty to display the blog posts as an embedded part of your Lofty website.

Depending on when you started with Lofty, there are two different ways to manage the blog: (1) using the Lofty-built blog editor or (2) using a WordPress blog editor which is only available for those that have joined Lofty prior to May 8, 2021.

 

Notice: The Starter package does not come with this feature. If you are on a Starter package and interested in using this feature to its full effect, please contact Support to get upgrade options.

 

Summary

  • (1) Lofty Blog Editor
    • Categories
    • Posts
      • Posts Overview
      • AI Blog Assistant
      • How to manually add a Blog Post
    • RSS Aggregator
    • Lofty Blog Editor FAQs
  • (2) WordPress Blog Editor
  • Blog Page Components
  • Customizing the Style of the Blog Page
  • Blog Editor Migration: WordPress --> Lofty

 

(1) Lofty Blog Editor

To access the Lofty Blog Editor, go to CMS >Quick Actions >  Blogs:

Your blog posts will display in the same order they appear within the posts list within the CMS settings. You can pin one post to the top, or you can sort the posts by published date or updated date to have those appear in that order automatically.

Categories

Use categories to file specific blog posts under specific groups so that you can easily classify and display your content for site visitors. 

 

Categories Overview

All the categories that have been created are available on the Category List:

  • Name: The name of the category
  • Blog Count: The total number of blog posts currently in that category

 

Add a Category

To add a category, click on the blue + Add New button in the top-right, add the category name, and then click on the green checkmark to add it.

 

Edit / Delete a Category

Click on the Edit or Delete buttons to edit or delete a blog category:

Posts

Posts Overview

View all posts, those that are published, drafts, or those that have been trashed, using the tabs at the top:

  • All: Includes those that are "Published" or "Drafts."
  • Published: Posts that are published and displayed live on your website.
  • Scheduled: Posts that are set to be published at a future date.
  • Drafts: Drafts can be edited in the back end but will not be visible on your website.
  • Trash: Posts that are deleted can be recovered or deleted completely.

The columns display the following data:

  • Title: The title of the post. A post with no title will show "no title," and any drafts will have a "Draft" tag next to them in this column.
  • Author: The author of the blog post.
  • Category: The categories of a blog post.
  • Publish Date: The format is mm/dd/yyyy and is based on the date the blog post was created. The most recent blog posts will be displayed at the top.
  • Updated Date: This is based on when the blog post was revised, adjusted, or corrected. 

AI Blog Assistant 

The AI Blog Assistant uses AI to help you craft blog posts seamlessly! Navigate to the CMS tool and click Blog.

Next, use the AI chat panel to tell the AI what you would like to write a blog about. The AI will give you a few prompts, or you can start fresh!

Once created, take a moment to review the blog, make any necessary edits, and decide when to publish!

 

How to manually add a Blog Post

To add a new blog post to your website, go to Posts and then click on the blue + Add New button in the top-right:

You will then be presented with the blog post editor window:

Content

Title: The title of a blog post. If no title is added, the post will display as "no title."

Blog Post Content: The body of the blog post. Using the tools available, you should be able to build the content out in the format you would like, including adding images, embedding videos, changing the styles, fonts, etc. You can even embed source code in the blog post if you have coding experience and would like to use the blog feature to display something unique. 

As you add blog content, you can preview how it will display in the panel at the right:

When creating a new blog post, you can now edit the line spacing and schedule a specific time for your post to be published:

 

Settings

The following are the settings that can be edited for each individual blog post. Click on the Settings tab to edit:

 

Author: The default author is always the owner of the website, but you can manually overwrite this if you would like to do so.

 

URL Slug

"URL Slug" refers to the last part of a URL that is specific to a web page. The default URL Slug is the post title but you can edit this without having to change the post title. The following are supported: letters, numbers, and hyphenated words (e.g. "first-blog-post"). Other characters cannot be recognized and will be changed into hyphens automatically.

 

Categories

This is where you will select the category that this blog post belongs to. Adding new categories is outlined above or you can add a new category directly in this field. A post can belong to multiple categories. A blog post that has no category selected will belong to "Uncategorized." 

 

Featured Image

The default featured image is the first image in the blog post content. The featured image for a post that does not have an image will be the logo from your website header. The featured image can be changed and/or deleted as needed.

 

SEO

For more information on SEO basics, you may want to reference THIS article.

To edit the SEO settings for an individual blog post, click on the SEO tab:

 

Meta Title: 

A meta title (also called a title tag) is an element in the head section of an HTML document that defines the title of each page of a website. It is retrieved by web browsers and also used by search engines such as Google to display a webpage in search results (SERPs). The default meta title is in the following format:

Blog Title - Creator Name - Company Name

This can be edited and you can use the tool to "+ Insert variable."

 

Meta Keywords:

Meta keywords describe the content of a web page in a short and concise way and should be important indicators of a page's content to search engines. The default meta keywords are blank when you create a new blog post in Lofty but you can add/edit as well as use the "+ Insert variable" tool if needed.

 

Meta Description:

A meta description is an HTML element that describes and summarizes the contents of your page for the benefit of users and search engines. The default meta description is the first sentence in the blog post but can be changed by editing and using the "+ Insert variable" tool.

 

Edit, Delete, or Recover a Blog Post

To edit or delete a post, click on the Edit, Delete, or Recover icons for a post:

 

You can now Recover deleted posts as well under the "Trash" tab:

RSS Aggregator

Find this option under CMS > Blogs Tab > RSS Aggregator:

 

Here is the information presented on the RSS Aggregator page shown above:

  • Name: The name of the RSS blog source.
  • Last Updated: Displays the last updated time as well as the number of items imported with the most recent import.
  • Imported Items: The total number of articles obtained from the feed.
  • On/Off: If turned on, articles will be automatically synced from the blog source one time daily at 7:00 am. If turned off, a sync button under Imported Items will have to be clicked manually to bring in the newest content.

 

When adding a new RSS feed, all of the following are visible: 

  • Name: The name of the RSS blog source.
  • URL: The RSS feed URL from the blog source. 
    • "Input the URL of the feed source. In some situations, the URL of the site will work, but for best results, we recommend finding and using the URL specific to the RSS feed. Be sure to also include http:// or https:// at the beginning of the URL."
  • Post Type: Not editable, will default to "Feed Source."
  • Post Status: Choose from "Published" (new RSS feed blog posts will be published automatically) or "Draft" (new RSS feed blog posts will come in as drafts and must be published manually). If changed, the status will only reflect on the next pulled post, not on previous ones.
  • Post Date: This will always be the original post date of the incoming blog content.
  • Remove featured image from post content?: 
    • Yes = The featured image from the incoming blog article will be removed and when sharing the blog post link on social media, the image will be the header logo (if available) otherwise, it will be the first image in the article or an image from the Lofty gallery as a last option.
    • No = The first picture of the article is selected as the SEO content so if the article is shared on social media that will be the one shown. If there are no images in the article, a default image from the Lofty gallery will be displayed instead.
  • Feed Preview: Displays previews of the five most recent articles available at the RSS feed URL. 

 

Lofty Blog Editor FAQs

How can I wrap text around an image?

1. Click Insert/Edit Image

2. Upload an image and click OK

4. Adjust the width and height of the image

5. Click Save

6. Add text below the image

7. Click on the image and click on Align left/right

8. The text will wrap around the image

 

(2) WordPress Blog Editor

*IMPORTANT: Please note that the WordPress blog editor will not be available to use if you do not already have it enabled on your account prior to May 8, 2021. You will still be able to add/edit blog content using the Lofty-built blog editor if you do not have access to the WordPress blog editor.

 

Lofty + WordPress Basics

Here is a video explaining the basics of how to access and use the WordPress/Lofty blog feature:

 

Changing Post Meta Title & Description via WordPress

Lofty uses a Yoast SEO plug-in to change the SEO title and Meta Description in WordPress. This will then be automatically synced to the Lofty website.

Log in, access a post, and edit here:

 

Blog Page Components

All blog page templates have the same basic components as seen in the screenshot below. 

  1. Blog Posts listed on the left side of the page
  2. A Search Bar that can be used to search for any keywords that are contained within the post titles or content
  3. Categories that synchronize with the categories created in the blog settings
  4. Recent Posts are shown on the right side as well

 

Customizing the Style of the Blog Page

As always, you can add, edit, and delete, blocks to customize your Lofty pages. To learn how to do so, please reference the following article: Add / Remove / Edit Blocks on Pages.

 

Blog Editor Migration: WordPress --> Lofty

If you are currently using the WordPress blog editor within Lofty to produce blog content, you will see a pop-up appear giving you the ability to trigger the migration of (a) all of your blog posts and (b) all of your categories from the WordPress Editor to the Lofty Blog Editor instead. If you have RSS feeds configured, those will not transfer during this process and will have to be set up manually. The migration should be complete in a matter of seconds, though that will depend on the number and complexity of the blog posts and categories. You will not be able to access the blog editor during the transfer process. If, after the transfer, you need to access your previously-used WordPress Blog Editor (to reference old drafts, etc., for example) then you can contact the Lofty Support Team (support@lofty.com) and they will be able to assist you by providing direct login credentials to WordPress.

*IMPORTANT: Once you have transferred from the WordPress blog tool to the Lofty one, you will not be able to transfer it back.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Add a Lead
title: Add a Lead
body:
Introduction

If you have a new lead that you would like to add to the CRM to communicate with them, track their progress, etc., this can be done by navigating to the People Page and then clicking on the "+ Add Lead" button:

Once you click the “+ Add Lead” button, there will be a pop-up window where you can input the lead‘s information. You must enter the lead’s first name when adding the lead. Remember that you can always go back and add/edit more details to a lead's profile after they have already been added. 

A few important things to keep in mind when adding a lead:

Privacy

Please reference the following article to learn more: Lead Privacy: Team Leads vs. Private Leads.

Phone Type | Status

If the lead’s number is labeled as landline/DNC number/DNC Contact, the lead will not receive any auto texts.

 

Property Address

The system will add a property to the lead automatically once you enter the address in this field.

When the billing address country is set to Canada, all address fields in the CRM will be updated to reflect the Canadian address format.

Note: This will not automatically mark all phone numbers currently listed on a lead’s profile as Canadian; however, all newly added numbers will default to the Canadian country code.

Source

The source will default to "Other," but a drop-down menu is available to select from any of the existing sources already in the database.

 

Custom Fields

Lofty supports using custom fields when adding leads. You can set up custom fields in Lofty settings, and then they will appear on the pop-up window for you to use. Please reference this article for more information: How to use Custom Fields.

Send Welcome Email

The system will send a welcome email to the lead with the login information for your IDX website. Their activity on the IDX website will then be tracked automatically.

Family Member

You can add additional family members to the lead if you have enough information. For more instructions on how this works, please reference this article: How to Manage the Family Members of a Lead.

 

Once all of the information has been entered correctly, click on the "Save" button to create your new lead!

 

Adding Agents as Leads

A user's email address can be used as both an agent/user login as well as an email address assigned to a lead. Admins may be interested in adding their new team members as a way to provide them with training via an automated Smart Plan that they have built out, for example. The email address can only be used once per team as a lead as well. 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or chat with us through your CRM.

 

Related terms: add a lead, adding a lead

name: Lead Pond
title: Lead Pond
body:
Introduction

The "Lead Pond" is a location for storing leads that are not assigned to a specific agent. Users given permission to use the lead pond will have access to claim leads and pull them out of the lead pond.

Some teams prefer to use this as an alternative distribution method instead of Next Up, Round Robin, or Blast Alert in lead routing rules. 

 

Summary

  • Lead Pond Setup
  • Using a Lead Pond
  • Claiming a Lead from the Lead Pond
  • Enterprise Lead Pond Permissions
  • FAQs

Lead Pond Setup

Currently, only teams under an Enterprise Lofty package have access to up to 5,000 lead ponds. All team accounts can create one lead pond. A Lofty team account owner can purchase a Lead Pond Add-On in the Lofty Marketplace or in the Lead Pond settings.


Team owner of Single Instance, excluding enterprise（because Enterprise package support 5000 ponds

There are three (3) available packages :

  • 1 Additional Lead Pond $50/ month 
  • 5 Additional Lead Ponds $125/month 
  • Unlimited (5,000) Lead Ponds $225/month

Navigate to Settings > Lead Pond to edit lead pond settings.

 

Setting to "Clear Assignees"

There is one setting that is configured and applies to all lead ponds that are created. This setting is the following:

 

 

Adding a New Lead Pond

Click on + Add New Lead Pond to add a new pond:

 

First, give the lead pond a name. This will be the name you will use to access this lead pond later or use in lead routing, etc.

Then, select the Pond Owner. This is a required field, and the same user can be used for multiple Lead Ponds, if your package allows for more than one Pond. 

If the lead responds to the automated content, their communication will be sent to the Pond Owner, as their email and phone were used to send content. If the Pond Owner does not have a virtual number, the system will use the Team Owner/Admin's virtual number, but the variables will still utilize the Pond Owner's information.

Next, decide if you want to set a custom email signature for messages sent to leads in the lead pond. If this is toggled off, the Pond Owner's email signature will be included in emails by default.

Editing the email signature is the same as elsewhere in the CRM.

 

Finally, select the users who should have access to this lead pond. Users who are selected here will be able to receive notifications and access the lead pond via the People page.

If you are on the Enterprise account type, you may choose whether you would like the lead pond to be accessible by (1) Group, (2) Agent, or (3) Agent Tag.

Team accounts allow lead pond members to be selected by: (1) Agent or (2) Agent Tag

If you choose either one of these options, you cannot mix it with the other. In other words, you cannot select an entire group to have access to a lead pond but only a few agents from another group.

Be sure to hit the blue Save or Add button when you have finished.

 

If you would like to edit the above information for a lead pond in the future or delete a lead pond, simply navigate back to Settings > Lead Pond and click on the "Edit" or "Delete" icons:

Using a Lead Pond

Notifications

Notifications can be adjusted under Settings > Notifications:

New Pond Lead Alert

When a new lead is added to the lead pond that you have access to, you will be notified via this notification.

 

 

Reassign Pond Lead Alert

If a lead is manually moved to the lead pond as an assignee, then it will notify all users with access to the specific pond where the lead has been moved. 

 

 

Note: Since Lead Pond is not a real agent who owns an IDX website, no property alert could be created for leads assigned to Lead Pond.

 

Lead Pond Access

Users who have access to lead ponds can do so via the People page in both the web and mobile app:

 

Lead Routing

If you would like to lead route to a lead pond, you can choose the Lead Pond distribution method and then choose which pond (you can only choose one) you would like to send the leads to as part of this rule:

 

You can also assign leads to a specific lead pond as part of the Default Rule which is the "catch-all" for lead routing:

 

 

To learn more about lead routing, please take a look at Lead Routing Rules.

 

Claiming a Lead from the Lead Pond

To claim a lead from the lead pond, enter the Lead Profile page and then click on the orange Claim Lead Now button at the bottom-left:

Lead Pond Claim Log

When a lead is claimed from a lead pond, the claim log will list when the lead was claimed and which agent claimed the lead. All agents who have access to the lead pond will have access to the lead pond claim log.

To access the Lead Pond Claim Log, navigate to the Lead Pond view on the People Page and click the paper icon next to Export Leads.

The lead pond claim log will only show the leads claimed within the last 30 days.

Enterprise Lead Pond Permissions

If you have an Enterprise account, you may need to delegate Lead Pond permissions based on the users' groups. Permission is available to delegate Lead Pond management rights to Groups, allow different Groups to manage their own Lead Pond, improve Lead Pond management efficiency, and not interfere with each other.

The Lead Pond permissions for Enterprise permission profiles are outlined below:

  • Lead Pond - User's Group
    • Allows the user to create/edit/delete lead ponds for their group and subgroups
    • Allows the user to manage lead ponds created by users in their current group, but not Lead Ponds created by users in a subgroup
    • Allows the user to access all lead ponds created by users in their group and subgroups
  • Lead Pond - Entire Company
    • Allows the user to create/edit/delete lead ponds for the entire company
    • Allows the user to manage all lead ponds created by users with the Lead Pond- Entire Company permission
    • Allows the user to access all lead ponds in the entire company

 

Lead Pond Tasks

When a lead is assigned to a Lead Pond, any remaining tasks on that lead are assigned to the Lead Pond owner by default.

 

Note: When a lead is assigned to a Lead Pond, only tasks that are generated by Company/Group/Team Smart Plans will be retained and assigned to the Lead Pond owner. All other tasks will be automatically deleted.

  • That is if a task was added manually or created as part of a private Smart Plan, that task will be deleted from the lead profile.

FAQs

  • Can I import directly to a lead pond?
  • If auto emails/texts are sent to leads in the lead pond, whose call/text package is used for that?
  • Can I access the lead pond via the mobile app?
  • I plan to mass import leads to the Lead Pond. Will I be getting a notification for each lead I import?

 

Can I import directly to a lead pond?

Currently, you are unable to import directly to the Lead Pond. If you have a CSV import that you would like to place into the Lead Pond, you would have to (a) import the CSV and then (b) manually assign all of those leads to the Lead Pond.

 

If auto emails/texts are sent to leads in the lead pond, whose call/text package is used for that?

If a lead is on a Smart Plan that is set up to send auto emails and texts, it will use the text package usage of the Team Admin/Owner. Keep this in mind if you plan on keeping leads on nurturing Smart Plan campaigns while in the Lead Pond as it will affect the available usage for the Team Admin/Owner. If the Team Admin/Owner does not have a text package, the auto text will be turned into a manual task instead.

 

Can I access the lead pond via the mobile app?

Yes, we do support the Lead Pond in the Lofty mobile app.

 

I plan to mass import leads to the Lead Pond. Will I be getting a notification for each lead I import?

An aggregate notification will be sent for every 500 leads, rather than sending 500 notifications.

 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Property Detail Pages
title: Property Detail Pages
body:
Introduction

There are two types of property detail pages (aka: listing detail pages):

  1. Property Detail (the listing is not sold yet)
  2. Sold Property Detail (the listing is sold, with "Sold" status).

These two types of pages can be edited separately:

 

Summary

  • Property Details Page
    • Edit "Detail Info" Block
    • Edit Nearby Schools & Properties (Map) Block
    • Edit Market Trends, Demographics, and Similar Homes Blocks
    • Edit the Form and Quick Search Blocks
  • Link Anchor for "Request a Tour" Feature
  • Breadcrumb for Listing Detail Pages

 

Property Details Page

The property details page is built using the following blocks, some of which are unique to the property details pages:

  • Detail Info
  • Nearby Schools & Properties (Map)
  • Marketing Trends
  • Similar Homes
  • Form
  • CTA

*IMPORTANT:

  • Currently, these blocks cannot be deleted or hidden. They can be reordered. You can add blocks to these pages but please note that when you add a block to this page that all the listing detail pages will display that same block because it is a page group. In other words, you cannot add blocks to specific listing detail pages--for doing that you would want to build a landing page to feature one specific listing and add/remove blocks as desired.
  • To better display all block styles, the data shown in the preview area to the right when in the CMS Tool is demo data. You can publish and go to the live site to see the actual effect.
  • If you are located in Canada, please see Feature Availability for Users in Canada

 

Edit "Detail Info" Block

To edit the first block, double-click or select the "Edit" icon on the detail info block:

 

This one includes the ability to edit the style by clicking the "Change Style" button:

 

Toggle on/off the option for "Auto-expand Listing Details":

 

To adjust the "Displayed Agent" information, use the three available fields. The option to "Priority Show Listing Agent" will make it so that if there is a listing agent that is on the Lofty team and it is their listing, it will display their information. However, this is only for the display of the agent information or co-listing agent information, but is not related to who the lead, messages, etc. go to. Lead distribution is set up via lead routing (Agent Lead Routing Rules). This is all set up using the MLS Agent ID that is in the Lofty user's preferences under settings. 

You can adjust the side CTA (Call To Action) with the available settings:

Change any registration trigger settings:

 

Edit Nearby Schools & Properties (Map) Block

The options to edit here include the title as well as the nearby setting:

 

Edit Market Trends, Demographics, and Similar Homes Blocks

These sections will only allow you to change the title, as data from the MLS and third-party data populate the rest:

 

Edit the Form and Quick Search Blocks

These articles, Form Block & Quick Search Block, provide more information on editing the "Form" and "Quick Search" blocks.

 

Link Anchor for "Request a Tour" Feature

This anchor was developed to take site visitors to the Request a Tour level on a listing detail page. If you would like a site visitor to be sent directly to that part of a property detail page, simply add #schedule at the end of your listing detail page URL so that site visitors can be directed to the "Request a Tour" option on that listing. 

Here is what it appears as on desktop view:

 

On the mobile view, the site visitor will be taken directly to a pop-up that looks like this one:

 

Breadcrumb for Listing Detail Pages

A "breadcrumb" (location hierarchy links) is available on every listing detail page. The format is the following: #State# > #City# > #Subdivision# (for Canada, this will be #Province# > #City# > #Subdivision#). All of this information is generated directly from the MLS. This will allow site visitors to easily find other listings in the city or subdivision without having to go back to generate a separate search. Please note that the state is currently not clickable.

This type of feature on every individual listing detail page also improves the usability of our websites and increases overall SEO value as well.

 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Content Block
title: Content Block
body:
Introduction

The "Content Block" is used for displaying basic text or images which typically includes a business description or the vision of the business, etc. This is a useful block to place on your page should you need to add text, images, videos, or HTML code. 

Summary

  • Adding a Content Block to a Page
  • Content Block Types
    • Rich Text
    • How it Works
    • We Are
    • Two-Columns, Two-Rows

 

Adding a Content Block to a Page

Click on the "+ Block" button on the Editor:

 

Choose "Content" from the Block Library, select the type of content block that you would like to use, and then drag it to the right side of the CMS where you would like to place it.

 

 

To edit the block, double-click on the block or select the "Edit" icon on the right side.

 

Content Block Types

Below are the different types of content blocks:

 

Rich Text

The first type of content block is Rich Text. This type is extremely flexible and can be used to insert text, images, videos, and even HTML or Javascript (front-end code). This block size is not ideal for large interactive content and is instead best used with static content that fits well in the space.

This is what this field will look like prior to editing: 

 

To edit, double-click or select the "Edit" icon of the block as indicated above. Then, select "Click to Edit Rich Text."

This view will allow you to edit the content, adjust text formatting, embed links, images, and even videos:

 

To add/edit code, click on the "Source Code" icon on the far right side of the editor. You can then embed your code as needed.

**Please note that if you insert code yourself, the mobile adaptation will also need to be considered within your code.

 

To learn more about adding custom code to your website, please see Advanced Website Customizations.

 

How it Works

The second content block type is called "How it works." This is typically used for displaying your business process for buying and/or selling. It has three columns for displaying the content (this cannot be customized). An image, title, and description can be added to each column.

Here is what this type looks like:

 

All of the options to edit this block will be available on the left side when you double-click the block or click on the "Edit" icon for that block.

 

We Are

The third content block type called "We Are" is similar to "How it Works" with the only difference being that it does not allow for the display of images and only displays text. The background type and color can also be adjusted.

Here is what this block looks like: 

 

 

Two-Columns, Two-Rows

The fourth type is a two-column and two-row content block. It is typically used for showing your business value or benefits that clients will see when working with you. You can define your title and four descriptions, as well as the background of the block.

 

Banner Block

The "Banner Block" is typically used to display a picture (or multiple, sliding pictures) or a video. It normally has text on top of it and including a heading and a subheading. 

For background settings, you can choose the "Background Type" (image, color, slideshow, video), desktop image, and mobile image. 

You can adjust the spacing before or after the block:

For "Block Size," you can adjust the desktop size type (aspect ratio, full screen, exact height) as well as the mobile size type (aspect ratio, full screen, exact height). 

For "Content Mode", you can choose what content you want to display, Agent or Heading and Subheading.
You can choose an agent to show their information.
Also, you can choose to show a heading and subheading. You can change the heading and subheading here. If you do not want to display any text here (e.g. a simple slideshow or standalone video), you can leave the heading and subheading fields blank.

 

Size Recommendations

At present, we have four sets of templates and each template image size is slightly different from the other. Also, the mobile view and the desktop view will vary. This section will provide the suggested sizes for each of these scenarios.

Image Background Type

For the "Block Size," we recommend leaving the default selection of "Exact Height" for both desktop and mobile.

Banner Style 1

Desktop Size Recommendation: 1440 x 460 pixels
Mobile Size Recommendation: 750 x 440 pixels

Banner Style 2

Desktop Size Recommendation: 1440 x 460 pixels
Mobile Size Recommendation: 750 x 500 pixels

 

Video Background Type

As far as file size, the video can be no bigger than 50 MB.

We recommend checking the box for "Auto-Adjusted Height":

For "Block Size," our recommendations are as follows:

Desktop View

Leave at the default values:

Mobile View

Adjust to the following:

  

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by a chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Landing Pages
title: Landing Pages
body:
Introduction

"Landing Pages" are a single page created specifically for marketing and advertising to bring leads in and get them to register. With the Lofty CMS, the ability to create high-quality landing pages is quick and easy to access.

All users on a Lofty account with an IDX website can access landing pages. Agents without a website will use the Team or Company Website to build landing pages. These users can create up to 10 landing pages. If the limit is exceeded, the user will need their own agent website or subdomain to create more landing pages. All leads captured on these landing pages will be assigned directly to the agent who created the page. The account admin can disable the user's access to build landing pages by turning off the Landing Page permission (see Organization - Permission Profiles).

 

Summary

  • Adding Landing Pages
  • Automatic Landing Pages
  • Recommendations
  • Editing Landing Pages
  • Sharing / Using Landing Pages
  • Registration Rules
  • Viewing Conversion

 

Adding Landing Pages

I want to let you know that the Landing Page functionality is not found directly in the CMS Tool. Instead, it is located in the "Marketing" section of Lofty. 

Click on "Landing Pages" from the options available on the left and then click “Add a New Landing Page” to start building a page:

 

The first step is to choose a page template to use. Page templates provide the basic page skeleton for you to edit and will also provide default blocks and content on the new landing page that you create.

Available Templates:

  1. All
    1. This is all of the Landing Page templates
  2. Listing
    1. Includes the following:
      1. Feature a Listing
      2. New Listings
      3. Open House Listings
      4. Price Reduced Listings
      5. Listing Search Campaign
      6. Multi-Property with Map
  3. For Seller
    1. Includes the following:
      1. Home Valuation
      2. New Seller Form
      3. Seller Guide Download
  4. For Buyer
    1. Includes the following:

      1. Featured Area Page

      2. Buyer Guide Download

      3. Live Tour (Standard Listing)

      4. Host a Live Tour

  5. Activity
    1. Includes the following:

      1. Lead Registration Form

      2. Meeting with leads

      3. Build Your Own

The next step is to enter the page URL / Page Name / Lead Source according to your preferences and campaign goals. The leads registered on this page will be added directly to the Lofty CRM and classified into the source defined in this setting. All of these fields can be modified later when editing the page.

Click "Save" and you will then be taken to the new landing page:

 

Automatic Landing Pages

Automatic Landing Pages are a feature that creates landing pages every time a new listing is added to the MLS. This requires that your Agent ID be added to your integrated MLS. It is also required to have an active Lofty website as well; this can be a team website, an agent website, or an agent subdomain. When a new listing is created, it will be generated as the "Single Property Promotion" template.

 

You will also receive an email alerting you to the creation, and also with the link to the new landing page.

 

 

To distinguish these from other pages in your Tools section. The automatically created listing will have an "A" icon at the end of the name of the landing page that was generated. 

 

You can disable this feature if needed at Marketing> Landing Pages> Settings  

 

Recommendations

A list of recommended (commonly used) landing pages is available at the top of the page. A landing page can be created directly from this list by clicking the button below the desired option. This menu can be hidden if no longer helpful. 

Editing Landing Pages

In the interface to the edit page, you will see three floating icons on the left (Settings, Style, and Block Library, SEO):

Settings

In this section, you can configure the following:

  • Basic Info
    • Basic Settings:
      • Page Name
      • URL
      • Page Style
      • Lead Source
      • Lead Type (leads who register on this page will come in as this type)
    • Lead Privacy and Assignment
      • Lead Privacy (see Lead Privacy: Team Leads vs. Private Leads)
      • Assignment Method (Directly Assign vs. Assign via Lead Routing Rules)
    • Additional Actions
      • Tag
      • Note
      • Send Welcome Email (yes/no)
      • Send Welcome Text (yes/no)
    • SEO
      • Meta Page Title
      • Meta Page Description
      • SEO Cover Photo (what displays when sharing a link to social media)
    • Chat Box
      • Show Chat Box (yes/no)
  • Page Tracking
    • Google Analytics Account
    • Facebook Pixel ID

Style

In this section, you can edit the theme color, title style, and button style of your landing page.

  • Theme Color. This consists of two parts: (a) primary color and (b) hover color. This includes all colors except the title and buttons. The primary color is the default color for most elements on a website. The hover color is the hover color of all clickable elements on the website.
  • Title Style. You can edit the title style of all blocks
  • Button Style. You can edit the style of all the buttons

Block Library

20+ block types can be added to any page by dragging and dropping the block to the right side. Each block type has different styles to choose from. If you want to modify the title, image, data, etc. of a certain block, double-click the block or click the "Edit" icon, and all of the content that can be edited on this block will be displayed.

For a full list of the blocks and how to use them, see this section in the Help Center: Block Library.

You can drag a block to the desired position by using the arrow icon.

 

When finished with editing, always remember to click on the "Publish" button in the top-right in order for changes to be reflected on the live website.

 

Sharing / Using Landing Pages

Share on Social Media (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn)

Whether you are on the interface to edit the page or on the page list, you can quickly share your landing page to Facebook, Twitter, and LinkedIn by clicking on the "Share" icon:

 

Share via Link

The direct link to the landing page can be copied and used in an ad campaign or on other social media platforms not currently supported to drive traffic to the landing page and obtain visitor registrations.

 

Share via Email/Text

On the Landing Pages section of the Marketing page, you can click on the "send" option to share the landing page directly to leads via email or text:

Upon clicking on the option to send a page, you will be able to filter out leads (200 at most) and send them via email or text:

Share via Chat

Click the LP icon to send a landing page to a lead directly via chat in the web or mobile apps. Use the search bar or filter to find the landing page you want to send.

Registration Rules

Landing page registration settings have been set up to make the transition to a redirected page work more smoothly. With this setting, the registration rules of the landing pages, a user can configure where registration is triggered.  This will allow users to better control the registration pop-up on this transition. 

 

*IMPORTANT: Please note that if you plan to test the registration rules (which is always a good idea), be aware that having the main IDX website and a landing page open at the same time and in the same browsing session, etc. will likely cause a conflict. Be sure to test using a new incognito window each time you test or be sure to clear the browser cache and cookies.

 

Viewing Conversion

You can view the conversion details and lead activities on each landing page directly on the list interface as seen below. The overview is not currently clickable, but you can filter by "Lead Source" or "Tag" directly on the People page if you have set those to register specifically for a landing page.

 

FAQs

Q: Sounds like the 10 Landing Page limit is in place for users with NO website, and either a subdomain or website user can have more than 10. 

A: Yes, users with a subdomain or website can create unlimited Landing Pages. 

 

Q: When building an Open House Landing Page, how does Lofty define “this week” (Sunday–Saturday or Monday–Sunday)?

A: When "This week" is selected, the search will show properties listed as available this week. The time range for "this week" is from Sunday to Saturday.

 

Q: If an admin logs in using the main account to create a landing page for a subdomain, will the setting be available like the ones in the parent site?

A: Landing pages created in the parent (main) site cannot be directly synced or copied to subdomain sites. Each subdomain’s landing page is managed separately.

 

Q: Is the build your own page option available for all packages?

 

A: The "Build Your Own" option is NOT available for all packages. The ability to create a blank landing page (i.e., a fully customizable landing page where you can add/remove blocks as you wish) is only available on upgraded website packages. Specifically, this feature is included in:

Vanity Domain Website

Full SEO Website

Team Website (with upgraded package)

Company Website (Enterprise, with upgraded package)

It is NOT available on the basic/free/agent website, only packages.
Users on these entry-level packages do not have access to the blank landing page option or are limited to pre-set templates with minimal customization.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please get in touch with our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM. 

 

Related terms: LP, landing page, custom page, promotional page

name: Lead Organization with Tags
title: Lead Organization with Tags
body:
Introduction

The main purpose of any CRM is to provide an organization above and beyond what can be done with a typical spreadsheet or contact list. In Lofty, this happens on the People Page and consists of Pipelines, Segments, Tags, and a variety of filters. This article will introduce Tag.

 

Summary

  • General Information
  • Manage Tags
  • Tag Management
  • Add / Edit Tags
  • Lofty Paid Lead Tags
  • UTM Parameters

 

General Information

The third level of organization with the People Page is done with tags. Similar to social media "hashtags," tags can be used for whatever purpose that an Office finds useful--providing a tool that can easily be searched later on for Office leads.

Every user can create their own Tags or lead an organization, and also utilize Tags in the Company or Office Tag Library. The entire office can use Company or Office Tags, but only those created by users with the "Office Filter" or "Company Filter" permission (see Permission Profiles). 

 

Manage Tags

A full list of all tags can be managed by doing the following:

  1. Click on Settings
  2. Navigate to Tags & Sources under the Features section
    1. If you do not have the "Office Filter" or "Company Filter" permission enabled, navigate to Tags
  3. Select the Tags tab at the top
  4. Add new tags, edit a tag to rename it, or delete a tag from your personal Tag Library.

With "Office Filter" or "Company Filter" permission enabled:

Without "Office Filter" or "Company Filter" permission enabled:

Tag Management

If you have the "Office Filter" or "Company Filter" permission enabled, you will have the Tag Management button. Any Tags added here will sync to all other users' Tag libraries. The lock icon keeps users from editing or deleting this Tag from their libraries. Office Owners' accounts have the same logic, but their Tag Management only includes their own Office Tags.

A Company/Office Owner/Admin can add Company/Office Tags to the Tag library by clicking "+Add New" above. There is a 100-character limit when creating a Tag.

Add / Edit Tags

To add tags to individual users, navigate to a lead profile and select the + in the "Tag" field of the Details section. If a tag does not exist, you can choose to create it:

 

You can also add/remove tags on up to 200 leads at once by navigating to the People Page, (1) selecting the boxes next to each lead, (2) clicking on the option to "Change Tags," and (3) selecting from the list, removing, or creating a new Tag. 

The following tags are built into Lofty by default: Open House, Text Code, and Lofty Paid.

Lofty Paid Lead Tags

All leads that enter Lofty from one of our marketing campaigns currently have the Source of “Lofty Paid Lead.” Now, with this update, Lofty users will be able to see whether they came from one of the following, in addition to that source: 

  1. LoftyPaid - Google
  2. LoftyPaid - FB
  3. LoftyPaid - FBform

 One of the above will be added as a Tag on the lead in addition to the source being Lofty  Paid Lead.

  • The tags can now be used for filtering specific sources even more granularly, Smart Plans, etc.
  • The tags can be added/removed manually if needed

 

UTM Parameters

See the following article for a full explanation of how to edit UTM settings: Lead Source Logic > UTM Settings. As to how this applies to tags, note that the following can be populated into Lofty as tags using UTM parameters:

  1. Import utm_campaign as lead tags. If a lead registers via a campaign or URL with an associated "utm_campaign," that campaign will be recorded for that lead automatically as a tag. A new tag will be created if it does not already exist.
  2. Import utm_content as lead tags. If a lead registers via a campaign or URL with an associated "utm_content," that content will be recorded for that lead automatically as a tag. A new tag will be created if it does not already exist.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your CRM.

 

Related terms: tags, UTM, UTM content

If a lead provides a Canadian address, they will not automatically receive a home value estimation. Instead, they will receive a message similar to the one below, letting the lead know that an agent will be reaching out.

name: Lead Organization with Segments
title: Lead Organization with Segments
body:
Introduction

The main purpose of any CRM is to provide an organization and beyond what can be done with a typical spreadsheet or contact list. In Lofty, this happens on the People Page and consists of Pipelines, Segments, Tags, as well as a variety of filters. This article will introduce Segments.

 

Summary

  • Edit Permissions
  • What are segments used for in Lofty?
  • Active vs Static Segments
  • Edit Segments
  • Changing Segments for Leads 
  • FAQ

Edit Permissions

It is important to note that only users with the Company/Team Filter permission (see Permissions) can edit the Segments by default. All users can add Tags and use the other filters. This means that the Segments are maintained at the Team/Company or Segment level and cannot vary by users within that Company/Team or Group.

What are segments used for in Lofty?

Segments are used for organizing and classifying your leads into different categories. Unlike pipeline stages, a lead can be categorized into multiple segments at the same time. You might consider creating segments for events, referrals, family and friends, years, specific reminder periods, etc. Segments are located in the People/Segments dropdown menu shown below.

Active vs Static Segments

A Static Segment allows you to add leads to the segment, and those leads stay in the segment until they are removed. Further, no other leads will be added to the segment, unless they are added manually.

An Active Segment adds and removes leads from the segment depending on your selected filters. For example, if you've added a filter for a specific lead score, leads that match the lead score will be added to the segment automatically, while leads that fall out of the lead score range will be removed automatically.

Edit Segments

Segments can also be customized to fit your workflow and team structure. The same segments will be available for the entire team and can only be edited by those with access. Click the "..." icon to edit a Segment.

There is also a "reminder" feature that allows you to set a specific reminder period for each segment, and if a lead is not contacted in that period, they will be marked as "expired." The green/red dots next to the segments indicate whether any leads have expired in that segment (meaning they have not been contacted within that period).

Hover over each segment with a reminder or check the Reminder column to see the "Expired" number and display those leads so that you can contact them. Once contacted, the reminder period will start over for that lead. 

When setting the reminder period, you have the option to decide if only manual touchpoints count or if automatic touchpoints also count as a lead contact.

  • When unchecked, only manual actions will count as lead contacts.

  • When checked, both automatic and manual actions will count as lead contacts.

Changing Segments for Leads

Just like with the pipeline stages, leads can be added to segments either individually or up to 200 at a time. To add individually, you can do so directly from a lead profile. Note that you can select more than one segment to be associated with the lead.

 

You can also add/change segments for multiple leads at once by checking the box next to the leads on the People Page and clicking the option to "Change Segments." This will add those leads to the selected segments. 

 

FAQ

Q: Are Segments the same as Tags?

A: Tags are generally used to classify leads that have the same characteristics. Tags are relatively simple, clear, and flexible, and are often used to group leads for easy searching. Segments are designed to group leads with similar characteristics into different categories to be used for business analysis and precision marketing.

name: Business Summary (Reporting)
title: Business Summary (Reporting)
body:
Introduction

In the Business Summary section, you have an overview of your team's performance within data reports, measured by many dimensions.

Summary

  • Team Transaction Data
  • Set Business Goal
  • Funnel Analysis
  • Lead Growth

 

Team Transaction Data

You can filter leads by time (year), type, segment, source, related tag, responsible agent, and transaction information together with the number of closings of all the transactions that are related to those filtered leads will be shown. 

The four kinds of transaction information collected are total volume, closings, gross commissionable income, and revenue.

Using the filters, you can sort through years and various other criteria, shown below.

Also, you can view the trend of the three types of money or the number of closings of all transactions as a month grows in the selected year.


Under Business>Performance by Agent, you can also view the total transaction information in each month separately within the selected year.

 

Set Business Goal

The Team Owner/Admin can set the transaction goals in whichever direction he or she wants to accomplish in the year. Click "Set Goal", then "Get Started," and finally, “+Start.”

The Team Owner/Admin can choose the money type for the goal and determine how the goal will be distributed (equally divide the volume to each team member, or set them separately).


After setting the goal, the Team Owner/Admin can compare the goal with the team's current performance, and get a sense of the pace.

If you are on the Enterprise account, the Company Owner/Admin is also able to divide the goals into groups:

At each office level, a Office Owner/Admin will be able to edit their contribution towards that top-level goal for each specific suboffice:

After the Office Owner/Admin has saved the business goal, he or she can view and edit the goal on the Settings-Goal page. For the Office Owner/Admin, you can view your entire agent team’s sales progress month by month. As an individual agent, you can only see your progress.

 

Funnel Analysis

The Team Owner/Admin can see the lead conversion rates between different states in the pipeline for the whole team or a specific agent, while the agent can only view his or her rates. The general view is shown on the "Summary" page, and the specific view is shown at the bottom of the "Performance by Agent" page. The conversion rate list for the agent or the admin is expanded by default, as shown below.

 

Rule of Calculation

For each state in the pipeline in the selected year, there are three numbers: historically entering the amount, historically out the amount, and current containing the amount, so we can calculate the coming in rate (current containing amount/historically entering amount), and coming out rate (historically out amount/historically entering amount), and these two rates should sum up to one.

There is also a Funnel Table that shows the two rates for each state in the pipeline for all leads in the team within the selected year.

Also, the admin can compare the rates for each state in the pipeline, specified by the agent, in a table view.

Note: Pipeline stage positioning matters. Stages AFTER closed do not appear on reports. A "lost" category should be added after an "attempting contact" category and additional layers via segments/tags built-in to track if it was a bad number, do not contact, etc.

 

Lead Growth

Scroll down to Lead Growth on the "Summary" page. Here, you have an overview of your individual or your team’s Lead Growth. Feel free to use the Zoom tab to see Lead Growth by week, month, quarter, or year.

name: Listing Filter Basics
title: Listing Filter Basics
body:
Introduction

Listing Filters allow you to be selective about the listings you want to display on your website. The listing filters put in place control the listings from all MLSs that are connected as well as any manual listings (formerly known as pocket listings) that you have added to your website.

*IMPORTANT: With the filter options, you can inadvertently keep listings from displaying on the “All Listings” section of your website. When adjusting the filter and criteria for “All Listings,” be sure that you do not remove all the listings by accident.

 

Default Filters

There are two filters provided by default:

  1. All Listings. By default, these will display all listings that are active and on the market. You can adjust the criteria to prioritize certain price ranges, locations, brokerage listings, etc. All property alerts are based on this “All Listings” category, meaning that if you remove listings in this option, they will (a) not display on the website and (b) not be sent in property alerts.
  2. Sold Listings. If the data is provided by the MLS, sold listings can be displayed in this section based on the criteria you establish in this filter.

To find these two filters, click on the CMS Tool > Listing Filters > All Listings / Sold Listings:

 

Custom Listing Filters

All custom listing filters are built directly into the listing pages and listing blocks (that make up a page). To learn more about listing blocks, please reference Listings (Featured) Block. More information regarding listing pages can be found here: Listings Pages.

This block can be edited by double-clicking the block or selecting the "Edit" icon for that specific block:

You would then select Listing Source > Use Custom Listing Filter. Normally, Lofty uses "All Listings" as the source for the block. However, if you need to create a specific listing set for the block. You can choose “Use Custom Listing Filter.”

 

Editing Listing Filters

When adding a new custom filter, you can select the Listing Type and the default sorting rule in the groups you set up. This sorting applies if you choose not to add any other criteria to a group. 

 

Group Settings

Within a filter, you can add multiple groups with specific criteria to prioritize and display those in Group #1 first, then Group #2, etc. This is how the order of listings is prioritized for each filter.

You can “+ Add Criteria” within each group, reorder your groups, or click on the trash can icon to delete a group.

 

*IMPORTANT: It is always best practice to check the “Listings Selected” to understand how many listings match the criteria that you are setting up in each of the groups. If “0,” this means that there are no active listings that match your current criteria within that group. If you are editing the “All Listings” filter, the last group should always have the remaining listings that you want to display on the site, but want to display AFTER the other groups ahead of it. You do not want to change this last group unless you no longer want these listings displayed on your website at all or have them sent via property alerts. This is a catch-all group that will display all listings after the other groups.

 

Filter Out Listings

You can add different criteria (the options available will depend on the MLS connected to your site) in each group to help you select the listings that you want to display. The following is a sample of the criteria available to you:

*IMPORTANT:

  1. If you check multiple checkboxes within criteria (e.g. Property Type), the relationship between each option is an "OR" relationship. For example, the listings selected with the criteria would combine all property types that you have selected (Single Family Homes + Townhouses + Vacant Land, etc).
  2. If you add other criteria within the same group (e.g. Beds), the relationship between those criteria and the others (e.g. Property Type) is an "AND" relationship. This means that the results would be fewer because it finds the properties that match the Property Type filter AND have the range of Beds selected.

 

Listings Preview

When all your filters are established, you can check the "Results" by clicking the tab at the top to make sure that the listings displaying here are the correct ones and in the correct order as well. The order would be determined by the order of the Groups that you have created.

 

Advanced Control Panel for Agent/Office Criteria

This setting is related to the "Sold" Listing Type only. Please reference the following article for more information on how this works: Advanced Control Panel for Agent/Office Criteria.

 

Save your Filter

After any modifications, do not forget to click on the blue “Save” button at the bottom. You can then publish all changes to the website and your listings will be displayed as filtered per your settings.

 

Questions?

name: Advanced Control Panel for Agent/Office Criteria
title: Advanced Control Panel for Agent/Office Criteria
body:
Introduction

This article is only to outline the Agent/Office criteria which are options in listing filters under the “Sold” listing type. If you are looking for documentation on how to use standard listing filters, please click here: Listing Filter Basics.

 

How the Criteria Works (using “Agent” as an example)

When you add the “Agent” criteria in your listing filter with the Sold Listing Type. You will see a “gear” icon next to it.

When clicking on the “gear” icon, you will see a control panel popup with four options:

  • Filter by both the Listing Agent and Buyer’s Agent. Display listings where the listing agent and buyer’s agent are the same person (that you select).
  • Filter by Listing Agent Only. Display listings where the listing agent is the one you set (whether it is sold by the same agent or not).
  • Filter by Buyer’s Agent Only (Default). Display listings where the buyer’s agent is the one you set (whether it is listed by the same agent or not).
  • Filter By Listing Agent Or Buyer’s Agent. Display listings where the listing agent or buyer’s agent is the one you set. If you choose this one, it also means the listings you display include all listings related to this agent.

*IMPORTANT:

  1. If you add multiple agents in the field, it will be an OR type of relationship meaning that it will be Agent 1’s listings + Agent 2’s listings, etc.
  2. Each group can have different settings selected by using the Advanced Control Panel as explained in this article.
  3. You can use these same guidelines to set up criteria by “Office” as well.

 

Don’t forget to save!

After any modifications, do not forget to click on the blue “Save” button at the bottom. You can then publish all changes to the website and your listings will be displayed as filtered per your settings.

name: Marketing Source Analysis
title: Marketing Source Analysis
body:
Introduction

In this section, you will learn how to view and compare how each lead source is performing using the Source Analysis report. 

 

Reporting Tab

First, navigate to the Reporting tab in Lofty. 

The Team Owner/Admin and agents who have the “‘Manage Team” permission will have access to this “Source Analysis” report, found on the Reporting page under Marketing > Source.

Here, you will see data regarding your lead sources with some relevant statistics, such as total leads vs. closed leads from each source. In this way, you will be able to see which sources bring in the most leads in your database. 

There are two views of this data: (1) Overview and (2) Table. 

Overview Tab

To get to the Overviw tab, go to Source> click the eyeball icon in the chosen source.
The “Lead Conversion” visuals in Overview show a comparison of the Total Leads and Closed Leads.

Table Tab

This displays a variety of different dimensions being tracked based on lead source.

 

Available Filters

There are two sets of filters available on both the Overview and Table format that can be used to better explore the data on the Source Analysis:

  1. Timeframe
    • This Month
    • Last Month
    • This Quarter
    • Last Quarter
    • This Year
    • Last Year
    • Last 2 Years
  2. Transaction Type
    • All
    • Purchase
    • Sale
    • Other

 

Key Definitions

  • Total Leads: This is the number of leads created in the timeframe selected.
  • Closed Leads: The number of leads, within the selected period, who have transaction(s) with the status set as 'Closed'
  • Valid Leads: Either phone or email is valid
  • Potential Leads: Leads associated with active transactions (not including Closed and Cancelled), that correspond to the time frame selected

Configuring the Reviews Block

Click + Add Reviews to add a new review:

name: Hero Block
title: Hero Block
body:
Introduction

The "Hero Block" refers to the first section that is typically seen on an IDX website with the large image, and text on top. Because of its prominent location on the Home page, this is an important block to configure correctly. 

Summary

  • Adding Hero Block
    • Background
    • Content
    • Search Section
  • Size Recommendations
    • Image Background Type 
    • Video Background Type

 

Adding Hero Block

The first block you will see on the Home page is the "Hero Block." Click the "Edit" icon on the top-right of that specific block in order to configure this block.

 There are three tabs in this block editor: (1) Background, (2) Content, and (3) Search Section.

 

 

Background

You can configure all of the settings for the block background here. Choose your preferred background type: (a) Image, (b) Slideshow, or (3) Video. When you choose "Image" as the background type, you need to upload the image both for desktop size and mobile size. If you do not upload an image for the mobile screen size, Lofty will use the desktop image instead.

When you choose the "Slideshow" type, you need to upload multiple images for desktop size and mobile size. If you do not upload an image for mobile size, Lofty will use the desktop images instead. You can then choose the transition effect (slide or fade effect), the slide transition time (in seconds) can also be adjusted here. The "Show Dots" will determine whether the noticeable dots display on the images so that visitors know there are more images to slide between. 

When you choose the "Video" type, you need to upload the video first. The Lofty CMS Tool supports YouTube URLs or uploaded MP4 files with a maximum size of 50 MB. After uploading a video, you can choose a video preview image in cases where you do not want to show the first picture of the video. After uploading the video, you can configure the video play settings:

  • Auto Play: The video will be played automatically if this checkbox is selected. If this checkbox is not selected, the video will only be played after the visitor clicks the play button that appears in the background.
    • **Please note that this setting only applies on desktop-sized devices as the video cannot autoplay in mobile browsers. 
  • Inline Play: This setting will only be shown when "Auto Play" is not selected. After selecting this option, the video will be played directly in the background when a site visitor clicks on the play button. If not selected, the video will be played in a pop-up after the visitor clicks the play button.
  • Auto-Adjusted Height: If selected, the block height will be adjusted automatically according to the video height in order to show as much of the video as possible. 
  • Show Progress Bar: If this is not selected, the video progress bar will be hidden. 
  • Show Mute Option: If this is selected, the mute option will be shown in the right corner.

You can turn on the "Different Background Type for PC and Mobile" in order to choose a different type for each device. This is ideal for video as auto-play does not work on mobile devices. 

 

The "Background Size" can also be adjusted in this block for both desktop device sizes and mobile device sizes. First, choose the size type. Lofty recommends the "Aspect ratio" type because it will be responsive for devices with different screen sizes. Other types available include "Exact Height" and "Full Screen." If you choose "Exact Height," you will need to define the specific pixel height.

 

The last background setting is that of the "Background Overlay." With this setting, you can add an opacity layer above the background. You are able to choose the color for this opacity layer.

 

 

Content

In the "Content & Search Position," section you can also choose the relative position of the content (heading and subheading) to the search section: Top-Bottom or Left-Right.

In the "Heading and Subheading" section, you can edit the content and style of the heading and subheading. Note that you can change the alignment of the heading and subheading in the text editor.

If you want to show an image (typically a team/company logo) in the heading and subheading part, you can change the heading type from text to image in the setting for "Heading Content-Type." The position of this image can also be adjusted as center, left, or right. 

 

Search Section

In the tab for "Search Section," you can edit the search section of the hero block. First of all, choose your preferred search style: None, Advanced Search Bar, Tab+Search bar, Button.

Note: Do not display any search options on the hero block. 

Advanced Search Bar: Choose the search fields that you want to display here. For now, the only options available are the following: Price, Beds, Baths, Property Type, and Purchase Type.

 

Tab+Search Bar: Define the default text in the search bar for the Sell My Home and Home Evaluation tab. You can also choose the name format and whether a name and phone are required.

Button: You can add up to four buttons at most. Edit the button text, style, and destination URL by clicking the "Edit" button for each button on the button list. You can also adjust the order of the buttons.

Size Recommendations

Mobile Size Recommendation: 750 x 500 pixels

name: Footer
title: Footer
body:
Introduction

The footer is a very important part of any website as it presents more company information, contact details, links to sites on the page, important MLS disclaimers, etc. Having this section up-to-date and ready to go is going to be an important part of building your Lofty website.

*Keep in mind that just like the website header, the footer can only be edited on the Home page via the CMS Tool. The steps to adjust this are found in this article.

There are four different styles to the footer. They will vary slightly with how the content is laid out and some of them might have two different background colors, etc.:

Summary

  • Edit Website Footer
  • Removing or Hiding the Footer

 

Edit Website Footer

On the Page Editor, navigate to the home page, scroll to the bottom of the home page, and double-click on the footer block or click on the "Edit" icon in the top-right of the footer block.  

To change the style, scroll all the way to the bottom of the footer settings and select the button to "Change Style":

You can adjust the background color(s) in the "Footer Background" section of the footer settings:

Make any changes to the "Sitemap Menu Style" including font weight, font size, font color, and hover color:

If there are any drop-down menus on your site navigation, you will need to adjust them here: 

One of the most important parts of the footer is going to be the display of any logos. Currently, you can upload up to five logos on the footer. You can also define the "alt text" and URL (when clicked) for each logo. If you want to change the order of the logos, just drag and drop using the option on the right side of each logo.

Choose the "agent" whose information (name, phone, email, address) should be displayed in the footer. That information is set up in CMS Tool > Settings > Team Info > Creator/Agent.

If you are an Enterprise owner or an Enterpriser user with a Manage Website permission, there is an option to display either the company name or group name or to customize the displayed content. The dropdown menu will display the company name and all the upper-level groups' names.

There is also an option to add custom content to a Lofty website footer. This is available on any editable Lofty website. The content added here will sync to any subdomains that are created off of this Lofty website. This feature allows you to add extra phone numbers, addresses, or other agent/office information.

Adjust the "Agent Name Style," "Agent Phone Style," "Agent Email Style," "Company Name Style," and "Company Address Style." All of these settings will include Font Weight, Font Size, and Font Color as seen here:

You can also add your own disclaimers to your footer by inputting any text or external links. Up to five disclaimers can be added to the footer. The disclaimers will be displayed under the agent info when using styles 1, 2, or 3 and under the sitemap when using style 4.

 

Removing or Hiding the Footer

For some pages, you might want to keep the footer from appearing in order to keep site visitors focused on the content of the page and avoid giving them access to additional content right away.

*IMPORTANT: With the footer, you need to be careful about when to hide it because it could take you out of compliance with your MLS. 

In order to remove or hide the footer, you will want to access the page editor and then select "Pages" in the top-left:

You will then select the "cog wheel" edit icon next to the page where you want to adjust this setting.

You will then be able to edit the setting for "Page Style" where you can choose whether the header and footer display or maybe just one or the other.

 

FAQ

Q:  Can I remove the copyright language "Made in Phoenix, AZ by your friends at Lofty Technologies, Inc. Copyright 2023 All Rights Reserved." on my account owner site?

A: Yes, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chatting with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Listing Blocks
title: Listing Blocks
body:
Introduction

The "Listing Block" can be used to embed a specific selection of listings on any page that you build. This can be ideal to feature your listings, office/brokerage listings, or a specific type of listings. These blocks are added by default to the Home Page as well as on Neighborhood Pages. The instructions to use this block type are found in this article.

 

Here is an example of what these blocks typically look like:

 

Summary

Adding the Listings Block

To add the "Listings Block," navigate to the page where you would like to add it and then click on the "+ Blocks" button:

 

Drag the type of the "Listing Block" that you would like to add to the right side where you would like it to appear on your web page. 

 

Editing the Listings Block

To edit the settings for this block, double-click on the block or click on the "Edit" icon in the top-right of that block:

 

Style 1

The first style looks like this:

 

In this style, the first thing to edit is the maximum quantity to display in this section before clicking on the "MORE LISTINGS" button:

 

You can then choose to select the listing source (All Listings, Sold Listings, Use Custom Listing Filter), any preset filters, and default listing sort.

 

You can also define what the text will say in order to view more listings (typically "View More Featured Listings"), the default view pattern (Grid, List, Map, Map+Grid, Map+List), map center point, default zoom level, and threshold for listings grouped on the map. 

 

Style 2

This is what the second style looks like:

 

In this style, there are three different versions that can be selected (V1, V2, V3) that will vary slightly in their appearance, the title can be defined as well as a description that will appear below the title. The maximum quantity to display can also be customized. 

 

Then, just like mentioned in Style 1, you can adjust the listing source, preset filters, default listing sort, text for more listings, view pattern, map center point, zoom level, and threshold for grouping listings on the map.

 

Style 3

Style 3 looks like this one here:

The settings to edit on this style are the same as with Style 2. There are more styles added to choose from shown below. 

 

Listings + Filters Help

For more information regarding how to set up the listing filters, please reference these articles: Listing Filter Basics and Advanced Control Panel for Agent/Office Criteria.

*IMPORTANT: Please note that selecting a specific listing source for a block will not affect the search results that a site visitor will see if they type into the search bar. In other words, the results populated by using the search bar on these blocks are not filtered by the custom listing filter (if selected). 

 

External Website Widget

For more information on how you can embed featured listings in another website (not Lofty-built), please reference the following article: External Website Widgets.

name: Home Valuation Block
title: Home Valuation Block
body:
Introduction

The "Home Valuation" block is a very useful tool for capturing seller leads on real estate websites. It will attract potential home sellers by giving them a free home valuation estimate for their property. 

  • Note: If you are located in Canada, please see Feature Availability for Users in Canada

There are two styles for this block that only vary in small details. On both, it will take two steps to capture the seller lead's contact information and home address and the third step will show the home valuation estimate to the lead.

Here are what the two styles look like:

 

Add the Home Valuation Block

 

Editing the Home Valuation Block

STEP 1

The site visitor will input their home address into the address box (they can choose from the Google address suggestions) and then click the button to the next step. In order to attract potential sellers and improve the conversion rate, you can edit the title and description that are shown at the top of the page. You can also change the background image(s)--this can be just one single image or multiple images (slideshow).

As for the button and search box style, you can adjust the button text and its style and change the color of the search box border. In addition, the placeholder text in the search box can also be edited, the default will be "Enter your street address."

STEP 2

After submitting the address, the visitor is required to provide their contact info to view the home valuation estimate for their property. Here is that step:

The title and description of the right side can be edited and you can choose your preferred name format (full name or first and last name) and whether the name and phone are required. You can also assign an agent that is active on your agent roster as well. 

 

*Please note that the email is required and cannot be changed to optional. The color of the "Next" button can be adjusted as well.

 

STEP 3

When the lead completes the previous step (#2), a home valuation report will be sent to their email and an estimated price of the address will be shown on the screen. Here is what that looks like:

You can edit the background color of this final set of data:

Lofty uses Bridge API (a company owned by Zillow) data to give the estimated price. If you do not believe that this price is accurate enough to show to your lead, you can choose "No" under the setting for Auto Home Valuation. 

If "No" is selected, the following will display and then the agent can reach out to provide a more accurate estimate with their industry experience and available resources.

 

Home Evaluation Report

After requesting a home evaluation via this feature, site visitors will receive an email that looks like the following (assuming the option to provide the home value is selected):
