name: Feature Updates for CRM 3.0.5, Site 3.6.9
title: Feature Updates for CRM 3.0.5, Site 3.6.9
body:
Introduction

*Please note that the features available to you on the Lofty platform will vary depending on the package you have purchased. For any questions in this regard, please reach out to your assigned Customer Success Manager or our Support Team for more information.

Release Date

The release date for this set of features is Monday, December 2, 2019.

Summary

  • Lofty AI Assistant
  • SkySlope Integration
  • Ability to Edit Notes
  • Partial Lead Permission
  • User Activity Log

 

AI Assistant

*The AI Assistant is an add-on feature and is not combined into any of the CRM/IDX package pricing.

Lofty is proud to announce that we have developed a built-in AI Assistant to support you by responding to and engaging leads both from your Lofty IDX website (via website chat) and from other lead sources (via text message). This AI Assistant will benefit your real estate business in the following ways:

  1. Shortening the time to first response and on a 24/7 schedule. New leads and website visitors will be engaged by the AI Assistant via website chat and text message within one minute--drastically reducing the chance of losing a lead to a competitor when you aren’t available.
  2. Help you focus on the most valuable leads first. The AI Assistant takes over the task of qualifying new leads so that you will be notified when there are serious leads ready to engage. The AI Assistant will also update lead preferences based on their responses to improve long-term nurturing. Leads with the wrong number or who are not interested will also be tagged as such.

The AI Assistant can be set up by navigating to Settings > Features > AI Assistant. This section will guide you through the options to set up the Lofty AI Assistant. 

For more information on how to add the Lofty AI Assistant, please refer to this Help Center article: How to Add the AI Assistant / Chatbot to your Account. More details on how it is used can be found here: Lofty AI Assistant / Chatbot.

 

SkySlope Integration

Lofty now has an integration with SkySlope for Transaction Management. Currently, Lofty supports exporting transactions to SkySlope, and additional features will be considered as they are made available in the SkySlope API. For more information on how the SkySlope integration works, please reference the following article: How to Integrate SkySlope with Lofty.

 

Ability to Edit Notes

Users can now edit notes that were made on a lead profile and are available on the timeline. There will be an "Edit" icon to the right of the note. Only the note portion of the logs can be edited. The notes can be edited by anyone with access to the lead even if they did not make the note. Editing notes will not change the timestamp of the note. 

 

Partial Lead Permission

A new permission has been added under Settings > Team > Agent > Agent Permissions > Partial Lead Conversion. 

This permission will limit the users who can use the paid-for service to convert partial leads by searching for data associated with an address. Only those who are given this permission can convert the leads and charge the $0.30/partial lead conversion to the Team Owner/Admin's card on file.

Those without this permission can still convert a lead by manually adding information, etc.

 

User Activity Log

Users with the "Manage Team" permission (see Team Permissions) can view a "Last Active" activity of team users under Settings > Team > Agent > Agent List. In this context, "Last Active" means the user's last operation time on Lofty when they opened a page or clicked a button in the CRM or mobile app. The system can only find data from two months ago. If users have not been active within the last two months, the "Last Active" section will be blank.

 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com> or by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557.

name: Set Up the Welcome Email
title: Set Up the Welcome Email
body:
Introduction

When a lead registers on a Lofty website, by default, they will receive an automated Welcome Email. This Welcome Email will provide them with their login credentials, allowing them to return to the website and access their saved searches, as well as continue browsing properties and additional content on your website. Aside from the website login credentials, you can edit the general content of this email.

 

Summary

  • Sample Welcome Email
  • Edit the Welcome Email
  • Turn Welcome Emails On/Off
    • Leads from Lofty IDX Website
    • Leads from other lead sources
  • Mass Send Welcome Emails
  • FAQ
    • Why does the Welcome Email only display the email address and not the password when I send it to a lead?

 

Sample Welcome Email

Here is what the Welcome Email looks like on the receiving end:

A few more templates in the automated emails section for the following lead types:

  • Buyer 
  • Seller
  • Renter
  • Investor
  • Agent Lead
  • Homeowner
  • Landlord
  • Other

Navigate to the Automated Email Templates by clicking Settings → Communication → Email → Automated Emails.

  • Welcome Emails
  • Click 'Show All' to see the new email templates:
  • Double Opt-In Emails 


    These emails have a pre-written copy, very similar to the other automated emails. The content can be edited by the user.

Edit the Welcome Email

The following portions of the Welcome Email can be adjusted--the rest is populated automatically using the login credentials for that lead as well as your profile information (see Complete your Lofty Profile for more information).

To edit this section, do the following:

  1. Navigate to the Lofty Settings
  2. Click on Communication> Email Templates on the left side
  3. Select Automated Email from the four options in the middle
  4. Click on the "Edit" icon on the "Buyer Lead Welcome Email" or "Seller Lead Welcome Email"

As a reminder, the headshot and contact information included in the Welcome Email to clients will be sourced from the information you have in your Profile settings. You can learn more about getting that set up in this article: Complete your Lofty Profile.

 

Turn Welcome Emails On/Off

Leads from Lofty IDX Website

The automatic trigger for the Welcome Email for leads entering from the Lofty IDX website can be adjusted directly on the same page (Settings > Communication > Email > Email Templates > Automated Emails > Toggle on/off in the "Applied" column).

Leads from other lead sources

This type of Welcome Email is turned off by default, but the status can be adjusted by navigating to Settings > Lead Capture > Lead Capture Settings > Toggle on/off in the "Send Welcome Email?" column.

 

Mass Send Welcome Emails

Lofty users can also manually send Welcome Emails for leads that are already in the database but have never received one. This option can be found under Settings > Email Templates > Automated Emails > Welcome Email. Keep in mind that this will not replace the standard process of auto-triggering a Welcome Email when a new lead enters the database.

*IMPORTANT:

  • This option will only send a Welcome Email for the leads where the current user (triggering the action) is in the assigned "Agent" slot for that specific lead.

When accessing this feature, there are two scenarios to be aware of. Hovering over the  "send" icon will explain: 

  1. "All leads have been sent login credentials."
    • All leads in the database have received a Welcome Email at some point in time. This means that no Welcome Emails can be triggered using this feature.
  2. "A Welcome Email is currently being sent for some leads. Try back later to review the status."
    • Welcome Emails are pending delivery. Check back later to make sure all Welcome Emails have been sent to your leads.

 

FAQ

Why does the Welcome Email only show the email address and no password when I send it to a lead?

This is because the lead has already received a Welcome Email at some point in time. The username (email) and password will only be sent in the first email. If the password is forgotten, the lead can always reset the password from the website using the "Forgot?" option.

FAQ:

Q: Why is my CRM not showing the "SEND MANUALLY" option?

A: Normally, this option can be found by navigating to: Settings > Email > Automated Emails > Welcome Email:

 

However, you may notice that for some accounts, the “Send Manually” option does not appear:

 

 

This may be due to several factors, including:

  • Opt-in requirements
  • Account creation method
  • Bulk sending restrictions
  • User permissions
  • Deliverability issues
  • Custom system settings

For example, if an account has a high bounce rate, Lofty removes the option to help protect overall email deliverability. If you need to enable this option, please check the lead’s opt-in status, review the account’s compliance and email settings, and confirm that you have the required permissions.

 

Note: The option to resend a welcome email to individual leads will still be available directly within each lead profile:

 

  

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Lead Import (via CSV/Spreadsheet)
title: Lead Import (via CSV/Spreadsheet)
body:
Introduction

Unless you are brand new to the world of real estate, you will likely have people you are already working with before joining Lofty. With that in mind, here is a brief description of how to import leads into the Lofty CRM.

We recommend using the sample file linked at the bottom of the article to configure your leads before uploading.

 

Summary

  • Important Notes & Suggestions
  • CSV/Spreadsheet Import Steps
  • Supported Fields
  • Reverse Option 
  • Import History
  • Importing to Lead Pond
  • Email Verification
  • Opt-In Probationary Period
  • Google Contacts Import
  • Import from Contacts (Lofty App)

 

Important Notes & Best Practices

  1. It is usually best practice to wait to upload your leads until after your Lofty website is live and working, in case you want to send a welcome email (see Set Up the Welcome Email) or set these leads up on auto property alerts (see Setting Up and Using Auto-Property Alerts). Without the website having the MLS data fully integrated, neither of those two options is possible. 
  2. Supported Sources:
    • Google Contacts
    • Spreadsheets in CSV, XLS, and XLSX (MS Excel) format
  3. It is recommended to do a test import of 2-5 leads as you begin to use this tool so that you can make sure they import correctly before importing a large number of leads
  4. If your spreadsheet has more than 10,000 rows, you will need to split the file and import it separately. Keep in mind that the bigger the file, the longer it will take to import.
    1. There is no limit to how many leads you can have in Lofty, but you can only import 10,000 rows at a time. If you have more than 50,000 leads to import, we recommend reaching out to support@lofty.com to request advanced import assistance. 
  5. If you try to upload the leads once but the import did not work correctly, you must go through and delete them all before trying again. To do so, go to the People Page select the leads to be deleted, choose "Delete" from the menu on the left, and then confirm. Then, you will need to go into the "Deleted Leads" section at the top of the People Page (this is like a "recycle bin"), to make sure they are completely removed from the system. If you do not erase them completely from the "Deleted Leads" section, new imports will merge or skip based on leads that exist there.  
  6. Admin/ Owner must create the pipelines prior to import for easier mapping later in the process. If a Pipeline is not similar to the one found in the import file it will be imported as a tag.
  7. If you want to move more than 5000 leads at a time from one agent to another, kindly reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your CRM.

 

 

CSV/Spreadsheet Import Steps

First, follow these steps to get to the right section in the CRM:

  1. Navigate to your Personal Settings
  2. Select Lead Import under the Lead Settings section
  3. Drag and drop your file or click Upload File to begin the import process

We simplify the import process and support the selection of different competing products. After selection, the competing product and Lofty fields will be matched automatically.

By default, the system will attempt to match the column names from the spreadsheet with the fields where the data belongs in Lofty. Typically, however, you will need to tell the data where to go in Lofty. You will do this by (a) referencing the column name and samples of the file which are available on the right side, and then (b) clicking on the "edit" option in the "Lofty Field Name" column to designate the destination of that data in Lofty. For example, you would want to make sure "Lead Type" matches with "Lead Type" in Lofty. 

Repeat the above process until all the columns from the document are matched to fields in Lofty. Even if all the fields show as "matched," you will want to review them to make sure they import correctly. When you come across a situation where no field in Lofty matches the data you are attempting to import, you have two options:

1. Import directly to a custom field. You can only create 50 custom fields that are either "Date" or "Text." See Custom Fields.

2. Import the data as a note. This will bring the column name into the note along with the data itself. This will then be saved to a lead profile for future reference. This information is not searchable.

 

Supported Fields

The following are all of the supported fields that you can import into:

General Options

  • Do Not Import. Use this option to skip a column.
  • Import as Note

Basic Info

  • First Name
  • Middle Name
  • Last Name
  • Full Name
  • Email
  • Email Description
  • Unsubscribe
    • Can be marked as any of the following three to mark as "Unsubscribed": yes/out/unsubscribe
    • If unsubscribed, the corresponding lead will keep automated emails (Smart Plan emails, property alerts, market snapshots, and market reports) from being sent to the lead. However, this does not affect text messages sent (see "Phone DNC Status" below for options there).
  • Phone
    • Can also be formatted with dashes ###-####-####
  • Phone Description
  • Phone DNC Status
    • DNC stands for Do Not Contact. Use this to mark a number as one to not contact. To mark as DNC, any of the following three options will work: yes/DNC/out
  • Pipeline
    • If the information within this field is not the same or similar to already-created Pipeline Stages, it will be imported as a tag. If you have the appropriate permissions, you should create any custom Pipeline Stages before performing a Lead Import. See more on managing and creating Pipeline Stages here: Lead Organization With Pipeline Stages
  • Segment
    • If you do not have permission to create a segment, the information within this field will be imported as a tag
  • Agent
    • Who the lead should be assigned to and who is a user of Lofty? Must be their name exactly as it appears in Lofty. 
  • Lender
    • The lender-type account to whom the lead should be assigned. Must be their name exactly as it appears in Lofty.
  • Mailing Full Address
  • Mailing Street Address.
  • Mailing City
  • Mailing State
  • Mailing Zip Code
  • Reg Date
    • Formatted as the following: 01/03/2019
  • Lead Type
    • Buyer
    • Seller
    • Renter
    • Investor
    • Agent
    • Homeowner
    • Landlord
    • Other

      To import a lead with a combination of Lead Types (i.e. both an Investor AND a Buyer), the lead type should be formatted as:
      "Investor|Buyer", separating the desired lead types with a vertical bar "|".

  • Source
    • If you do not have permission to create a source, the information within this field will be imported as a tag. Also, if no source is defined in the import, the default source will be "CSV Import"
  • Tag
  • Birthday
    • Formatted as the following: 01/03/2019
  • Seller Timeframe
    • Seller leads only. Based on the number of months.
    • Options:
      • N/A
      • 0-1
      • 1-3
      • 3-6
      • 6-12
      • 12+
      • Just Looking
      • Refinancing
  • Buyer Timeframe
    • Buyer leads only. Based on the number of months, it can be any one of the following:
    • Options:
      • N/A
      • 0-1
      • 1-3
      • 3-6
      • 6-12
      • 12+
      • Just Looking
      • Refinancing
  • Pre-Qualified
    • N/A
    • Yes
    • No
  • Family Member
    • Up to four family members can be added
    • Fields:
      • Family Member First Name
      • Family Member Last Name
      • Family Member Full Name
      • Family Member Email
      • Family Member Phone
        • Can also be formatted with dashes ###-####-####
      • Family Member Birthday
        • Formatted as the following: 01/03/2019
  • Inquiries (for a buyer)
    • Also known as "Search Criteria" 
    • Fields:
      • Inquired City
        • If you would like to add more than one zip code, please separate each of them with a vertical bar: " | ". For example: City1|City2|City3|City4. The city will line up with the states if you add multiple so in this example, City3 would line up with State3.
      • Inquired State
        • If you would like to add more than one zip code, please separate each of them with the vertical bar: " | ". For example: State1|Stat2|State3|State4. The state will line up with the cities if you add multiple so in this example, State1 would line up with City1.
      • Inquired Zip Code
        • If you would like to add more than one zip code, please separate each of them with a vertical bar: " | ". For example 11111|22222|33333|44444. The zip code will be added separately from the city/state.
      • Inquired County
      • Max Price
      • Min Price
      • Avg./Median Price
      • Min Bedroom
      • Min Bathroom
      • Property Type
        • Single Family Home
        • Townhouse
        • Manufactured Home
        • Vacant Land
  • Property Info (Selling)
    • Up to two properties can be added
    • Fields:
      • Property Full Addr.
      • Property Street Address
      • Property City
      • Property State
      • Property Zip Code
      • Price
      • Bedroom
      • Bathroom
      • Property Type
        • Single Family Home
        • Townhouse
        • Manufactured Home
        • Vacant Land
  • Property Info (Buying)
    • Up to three properties can be added.
    • Fields:
      • Property Full Addr.
      • Property Street Address
      • Property City
      • Property State
      • Property Zip Code
      • Price
      • Bedroom
      • Bathroom
      • Property Type
        • Single Family Home
        • Townhouse
        • Manufactured Home
        • Vacant Land
  • Custom Fields. Reference Custom Fields.

Click on the blue "+" to add additional slots for Family Members, Property Info (Selling), and Property Info (Buying). Limits to how many of each can be added are noted above.

 

Once you have matched up all of the columns and have everything mapped to the desired location in Lofty, click on the "Next" button in the bottom right.

 

You will be presented with the following options to choose from.

  • Select the ownership level. Leads can be imported as your Personal leads or to a Company or Office that you are a part of. 
  • Add the imported leads to a Segment. 
  • Assign unmatched leads to a specific Agent or Lead Pond. 
  • Assign unmatched leads to a Lender.
  • Choose to Merge or Skip duplicate leads.
    • If merged, the incoming data will merge and be saved as a note on that lead profile. 
    • For the logic on merging, please reference Duplicate Leads + Merging Duplicates.
    • If skipped, the duplicate lead data will not be imported.

  • Decide whether to send Welcome Emails to these imported leads or not. If you choose yes, you will want to make sure your IDX Website is up and ready with MLS data, etc. This will send out an email with that lead's login information so that they can connect to your Lofty IDX website and begin browsing listings.
  • Choose to apply Auto Property Alerts if so desired. These will be based on any property information that comes in during the import.

When you are ready, you can select "Confirm." The file will then begin importing. If it is a large document, it might take some time to complete. You will receive a notification via email and a web push notification letting you know the file import has been completed. 

Reverse Option 

When importing leads, there is often a need to reverse the import and remove the leads that were created because the import was done incorrectly, etc. Lofty allows users to reverse their import after one has already been processed as long as it is within 30 days of actually importing the leads. This option is available under Personal Settings > Lead Settings > Lead Import > Import History > Reverse. 

This will work regardless of whether the leads have been contacted, etc. The option will no longer be available after 24 hours of processing the import. The leads will be deleted completely from the system with this option--meaning they will not be sent to the "Deleted Leads" section of the People page. 

*For merged leads, they will stay in the system just as imported--the data imported/merged cannot be reversed if it was merged to an existing lead.

 

Import History

You can review all leads that failed to import by navigating to Settings > Lead Import and then selecting the "Details" hyperlink next to the file that you want to download a report on. This is a great way to make sure that everything makes its way into Lofty correctly. 

 

Email Verification

If the lead was imported in a CSV file, the Lofty system will call a third-party API to determine the validity of the lead's email address. We will mark the lead's email status as "Bounced" if the results provided by the third party indicate that it is an "invalid email." The accuracy level of this third-party API is typically between 90% - 97%.

 

Opt-In Probationary Period

If, when importing leads, you see an option to "Send opt-in emails to the leads" under the  Lead Import Settings options before finalizing the import, this is due to a high email bounce rate and an opt-in probationary period being triggered. You can learn more about this process here.

 

Google Contacts Import

Please reference the following article: Lead Import (via Google Contacts).

 

Import from Contacts (Lofty App)

title: Lead Capture - Listings to Leads
body:
Introduction

This article will review how to set up email parsing in Lofty for Listings to Leads. 

 

What kind of Email will be Parsed?

Lofty is able to parse a new lead into your CRM based on an email alert that comes from Listings to Leads to your Lofty-integrated email. Here are the common items that Lofty searches for in Email Parsing:

 

Lead Notification 1 -

From Address: donotreply@listingstoleads.com
Subject: Another Listings-to-Leads LEAD: Buyer Lead for xxx(address)
Email Body: 

 

Lead Notification 2 -

From Address: donotreply@listingstoleads.com
Subject: Request to know about Coming Soon home: Call For Address, xxx (City) 
Email Body: 

 

How to Set it Up

 Login to Listings To Leads homepage: https://www.listingstoleads.com/

Once logged in, click Profile. On the Profile page, scroll down to the Contact Details section and input your integrated email address (in Lofty) in the "Alternate Email" field (see screenshot below).

In the Send Leads To column, select the checkbox next to the Alternate Email field where your email address is entered. Scroll to the bottom of your Profile page and click Update & Save.

 

Note: The fields parsed from Listings to Leads are Full Name, Email, and Phone. Any other fields will be parsed as Note in Lofty. 

 

How to find your unique Lofty email address in Lofty?

Go to the Settings page, and under the Features section on the right, click Integration to Integration page and then click Lead Capture.

On the bottom of this page, you will see Auto-import Lead via third-party providers. Here, you will see your Lofty email, which you will use to auto-import leads from Realtor.com. In this section, click Copy.

name: Advanced Website Customizations
title: Advanced Website Customizations
body:
Introduction

If you have front-end development experience and knowledge and want to get more in-depth with your website customizations, this article will provide you with the basic information you need to get started when using the Lofty CSM to do this. 

There are three levels at which you can perform advanced customizations on your Lofty-built website--all of which are explained in detail in the sections below. Depending on what you want to accomplish (integrating a third-party widget, modifying a page's style, etc.), you will want to understand what is available at each level. 

 

Notice: The Starter package does not come with this feature. If you are on a Starter package and interested in using this feature to its full effect, please contact Support to get upgrade options.

 

Summary

  1. Global Customizations
  2. Website Currency
  3. Page Customizations
  4. Block Customizations

 

Global Customizations

To establish global customizations on your Lofty-built website, navigate to the CMS > Settings > Tools. You should be able to click here to get there as well (assuming you are signed in). 

 

This type of customization is divided into two different areas: (a) styles and (b) scripts--both of which are explained in more detail in their corresponding section below.

 

(a) Global Styles

Styles influence a page's layout, structure, color, shape, etc. Scripts can greatly enhance the visual aspects of static web pages.

  • Add document.head to the link tag embedded.
  • Write style directly. For example, use h1{color:red;} rather than <style>h1{color:red;}<style>.

 

(b) Global Scripts

An example of when you might use scripts is if you need to embed a piece of code to track your site's conversion. 

Run the new Function('siteAppVm', customcode.script)(siteAppVm) each time you enter the page. This can be used as an immediate function.

  • The script content is the function body
  • The properties defined in the function body are not globally accessible
  • The function parameter is siteAppVm (explained in the global object)

 

For example, to globally define a method foo() that fires when a button is clicked, you would do the following.

Custom Style & Script / Script:

window.foo(){
console.log('hello, world')
}

Button to trigger:

<a href="javascript:foo();">WELCOME!</a>

 

Global Object

(1) siteAppVm

SiteAppVm is a Vue instance mounted on the document.querySelector('main.page-content') element.

 

moduleData

ModuleData is an array [{name: module 1,data:{}},{name: module 2,data:{}}]. Objects are modules on the page in the array. Modules are displayed from top to bottom on the page. Depending on the dynamic binding technology, you can modify the moduleData in the moduleData to modify the content display of the module.

// Suppose siteAppvm. moduleData[0] is a header module
// Change the size of the logo to 300
siteAppVm.moduleData[0].data.size = 300

 

(2) Util

(a) addStyle(css, async=true)

Function: Add link tag in document.head

Usage: Util.addStyle(css:String, async:Boolean)

Parameters:

CSS:

If the CSS string contains '.css', then regard it as a link. For example:

Util.addStyle("//static.chimeroi.com/servicetool-temp/example.css", true)

Or the CSS string refers to the content of the style like this:

Util.addStyle(".red{color:red;}", true)

 

Async:

 - True: This means that the return of the Util.addStyle() the function is Promise, which means the CSS code has been completely loaded on this page.

- False: This means that the return of the Util.addStyle() function is a link element that loads the CSS code in the document.

 

(a) Example: How to introduce a Google font link: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Sofia

Because this is a link without '.css', then a '&name=sofia.css' suffix needs to be used to let Util.addStyle() function by regarding it as a link.

Util.addStyle("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Sofia&name=sofia.css")

 

(b) addScript(url, async = true)

Function: Add script code in document.body

Usage: Util.addScript(url: String, async: Boolean)

Parameters:

URL:

A link to the script page

 

Async:

- True: This means that the return of the Util.addScript() function is Promise, which means the JavaScript has been completely loaded. If the script was cached, then it will use cache.

- False: This means that it will insert the external link script in <head> instead of using cache.

 

(b) Example: Run certain functions after some JavaScript has been loaded completely.

Util.addScript('//www.example.com/1.js').then(_=>foo())

It is necessary to run the script again each time a new page is reached instead of using the cache. Suppose the content of this link https://www.example.com/1.js is as follows:

console.log('welcom to visit', location.pathname)

The control center needs to publish the path of the current page each time it is reached.

Util.addScript('//www.example.com/1.js', false)

 

(c) toast(text, delay = 1000)

Usage: Util.toast(text:String, delay: Number)

Example: Util.toast('hello', delay: 2000). With this function, a hint of 'hello' will show on the current page and disappear two seconds later.

 

(d) isMobileSize(size = 600)

Usage: Util.isMobileSize(Number)
Example: Util.isMobileSize(700). Used to determine whether the screen width is less than 700px.

 

(e) Util.login(options)

Function: Pop up a login box

Attributes in options:

Attributes
Type
Function
allowClose
Boolean
Whether a close button is permitted
showFacebook
Boolean
Whether to allow the site visitor to log in with a Facebook account or not
showGoogle
Boolean
Whether to allow the site visitor to log in with a Google account or not

Example: Pop up the login box with a close button.

Util.login({allowClose: true})

 

(f) Util.register(options)

Function: Pop up a registration box
Attributes in options:

Attributes
Type
Function
allowClose
Boolean
Whether a close button is permitted
showFacebook
Boolean
Whether to allow the site visitor to register with  a Facebook account or not
showGoogle
Boolean
Whether to allow the site visitor to register with a Google account or not

Example: Pop up the forced registration box without a close button and using a Google account to register is not allowed.

Util.login({allowClose: false, showGoogle: false})

 

(3) siteAxios

The siteAxios points to the module [axios](https://github.com/axios/axios).

 

Using the axios module to intercept a request and modify the request parameters:

// Add a request interceptor
window.siteAxios.interceptors.request.use(
function (config) {
// Do something before request is sent
return config;
},
function (error) {
// Do something with request error
return Promise.reject(error);
}
);

 

Using the axios module to intercept a response and modify the response data:

// Add a response interceptor
window.siteAxios.interceptors.response.use(
function (response) {
// Any status code that lie within the range of 2xx cause this function to trigger
// Do something with response data
// For example:
var config = response.__config__;
var addHouse = /api-site\/sell\add-house/;
var register = /api-site\/leadRegister;
if (config && (register.test(configurl) || addHouse.test(config.url))) {
debugger
}
return response;
},
function (error) {
// Any status codes that falls outside the range of 2xx cause this function to trigger
// Do something with response error
return Promise.reject(error);
}
);

 

Website Currency

This setting allows Lofty users to change the default currencies on their Lofty websites. Visitors to these websites can also change the currency displayed.

To access this setting, navigate to CMS -> Tools -> Language/Currency. There is an option to sync currencies to agent subdomains, but subdomains cannot set their own currencies.

We currently support the following currencies:

  • US Dollar
  • Canadian Dollar
  • Euro
  • Pound Sterling
  • Chinese Yuan
  • Japanese Yen

Visitors to the website can easily change the currency:

The currency will change in the following sections:

  • Listing/Sold prices
  • Home Valuationvalues
  • Mortgage Calculator

Page Customizations

To establish global customizations on your Lofty-built website, first navigate to the CMS > Page Editor > Pages:

 

Once you have clicked on Pages, select the setting wheel for the page you would like to add customize to. The screenshot below shows the Home Page being selected, but you can choose the page that you want to apply the customization to.

 

Then, scroll down and select the drop-down menu for Page Style & Script:

 

This type of customization is also divided into two different areas: (a) styles and (b) scripts. Both are explained below.

 

(a) Page Styles

Page styles influence the current page's layout, structure, color, shape, etc.

 

The page style will only apply to the current page. You can add it to the page by using Util.addStyle(pageStyle, false).

 

Write style directly. For example, use h1{color:red;} rather than <style>h1{color:red;}<style>.

 

(b) Page Scripts

Page scripts can significantly enhance the current static page. You may consider using page scripts when you need to embed a script to track certain conversion data on the current page. 

 

Page scripts will only run on the current page. Similar to what is outlined above for Global Scripts, the page scripts also run by using new Function(pageScript).call(siteAppVm). But the 'this' pointer points to siteAppVm.

 

Block Customizations

There are two block types available in the Lofty CMS that can be utilized to embed custom code. Please reference the two articles below to learn more:

  • Content Block
  • Code Block

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

Related term: custom style, custom script

name: Feature Updates for CRM 3.0.4, Site 3.6.8
title: Feature Updates for CRM 3.0.4, Site 3.6.8
body:
Introduction

*Please note that the features available to you on the Lofty platform will vary depending on the package you have purchased. For any questions in this regard, please reach out to your assigned Customer Success Manager or our Support Team for more information.

Release Date

The release date for this set of features is Monday, November 18, 2019.

Summary

  • Market Snapshot (replaces Seller Alert)
  • Smart Plan Improvements
  • Lead Pond Improvements

 

Market Snapshot (replaces Seller Alert)

Two notable changes have been made with this update:

  1. "Seller Property Alert" is now called "Market Snapshot." All current seller property alerts will be transferred to the "Market Snapshot" section.
  2. Market Report (by "subdivision" only) has moved to the Market Snapshot feature. The main reason for this change is a noticeable lack of MLS data for the format of Lofty Market Reports at the subdivision level. In order to provide data for subdivisions, all current subdivision market reports will be transferred to the Market Snapshot feature.

A "Market Snapshot" can be seen as a simplified CMA (competitive market analysis). The fields available when setting up a Market Snapshot are the same as when setting up a Seller Alert previously. In the email received by a lead, listings are categorized by listing stats (sold, pending, etc). A Market Snapshot can also be added for buyer/renter leads.

Here is what the content of this email looks like:

After clicking on any of the "View More" or "Check More Details" buttons for additional information, a lead will be taken to a new Market Snapshot landing page which will display more information for the specific area they are looking at. If the email is old, the Market Snapshot landing page will still display the newest information. Here is the what page looks like:

 

Smart Plan Improvements

Support for Birthday Smart Plans for Family Members

When applying a birthday Smart Plan to a lead, it will be activated on all family members who have a birth date listed on their profile separately. The auto emails and auto texts in each Smart Plan will only be sent to the family member whose birthday it is. The variables in each of the Smart Plans will use the info of the family member whose birthday it is.

Manual Task Reminders

Lofty users can now set up a reminder for each manual task in a Smart Plan (with the exception of "Checklist") to remind the assignee of the task. The remainder can be sent via an automated phone call or automatic text message when/before the task is due.

*Please note that a call/text package is required in order for the reminder feature to work as the call/text will be made via the virtual number. If the Smart Plan is a "Team Smart Plan," the reminder call/text will come from the Team Admin/Owner's virtual number. If it is a "My Smart Plan," the reminder call/text will come from that specific user's virtual number. This will count as call/text package usage. A call package (add-on) is required for call reminders.

You can be reminded by call or text at one of the following times: 

  • When the task is created
  • 5 minutes before due
  • 15 minutes before due
  • 1 hour before due
  • 1 day before due 

Here is a sample of the content in the text message: "Hi, you have a new task for [lead name] at [task due time]. The task description is [task description]. Check your Lofty CRM for further details."

A sample phone call is attached at the bottom of this article.

 

Lead Pond Improvements

New Permission

A new permission has been added that allows the Team Owner/Admin of an account to determine who should have access to the lead pond. Access includes putting leads in the lead pond, taking leads out, and viewing leads in the lead pond. This setting is located under Settings > Team > Agent > Agent Permissions. 

Clear Assignees

An additional setting has been added to those who have access to the lead pond settings (users with the "Team Management" permission). This setting will allow for an option to be selected to clear all "Assigned To" roles (except the lender role) when a lead is assigned to the lead pond. This setting is located under Settings > Features > Lead Pond.

 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com> or by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557.

name: Lead Export
title: Lead Export
body:
Introduction

Lofty provides a built-in export feature that allows you to export a CSV copy of the leads and contacts in your Lofty database.

Please note that exporting the leads from the CRM does not mean you are erasing them from your database, you are technically just securing a copy of the contacts.

*This feature can only be used by those who have been given access. For more information regarding permission, please reference this Help Center article: Permission Profiles.

 

Summary

  • How to Export
  • Exporting Personal Leads
  • Sample Export File

 

How to Export

After selecting the leads to export. Navigate to People>  click the 3 dots beside the Add Lead button > Lead Export. 

After clicking on the "Export" button in the bottom right, you will receive an email when the export CSV file is ready. There is a hyperlink in the export email that can be clicked to actually download the CSV. Make sure to click the link in order to obtain the document as the CSV will not be attached to the email itself.

If you do not immediately receive the email, consider checking your spam folder and wait 10-15 minutes. Depending on the size of the export, the file might take longer to deliver.

In the CRM, you will find it in the Notification window under Leads Alert.

Exporting Personal Leads

Agents who own Personal Leads (see Lead Privacy: Team Leads vs. Personal Leads) do have the ability to export these via CSV as long as they are the owner. An agent cannot see nor export private leads that belong to someone else.

 

Sample Export File

A sample export CSV file can be found at the bottom of this document. No data is shown in the file, but the column names will be the same when you request your export.

 

 

Questions?

name: Setting Up and Using Auto Property Alerts
title: Setting Up and Using Auto Property Alerts
body:
Introduction

 

If you receive a large number of new leads daily, it can be challenging to manually set up property alerts for each one. Lofty can help automate this process! The Lofty Auto Property Alerts feature sets up property alerts for new leads based on their initial inquiry and updates according to their search criteria and behavior on your IDX website.

For best results, the Auto Property Alerts feature is turned on by default for Buyer Property Alerts and Market Snapshots, but off for Market Reports. You can turn these off or adjust the settings at any time.

 

Summary

  • Settings Location
  • Turn On / Off, Deleting Existing Auto Alerts
  • Auto Alert Settings
  • Reviewing Auto Property Alerts on Leads
  • Requirements for Auto Alerts
  • Frequency of Alert Emails

Settings Location

Navigate to Automation > Auto Property Alerts to set up automated property alerts. 

 

Turn On / Off, Deleting Existing Auto Alerts

To turn on Automated Property Alerts, check the box next to "Enable" and then click "Apply" on the bottom right. If you are a Team Leader/Admin and want the settings to be applied to all the team users, check the box next to "Apply for the team" before clicking "Apply."

*Important: Auto Property Alerts for buyers and sellers need to be turned off separately.

 

If you disable the auto property alerts by unchecking the box, you will have the ability to delete existing alerts. Note that if you choose to do so by clicking on the hyperlink, you will only be deleting all existing auto property alerts. Manually created property alerts will not be affected.

Auto Alert Settings

Exclude Source

  • This setting allows you to deactivate Automated Property Alerts, Market Snapshots, and Market Reports, based on the lead's Source. 
  • Checking the box next to the source will deactivate that Source for these automated alerts. That is, leads from that Source will not receive the alert emails. 

Exclude Pipeline

  • This setting adjusts when auto alerts are APPLIED to new leads in the system.
  • This setting does not remove auto alerts. If a lead is imported to the database or added directly to a pipeline stage that is on this exclusion list, it will not have auto property alerts applied. However, if a lead already has an auto property alert applied, it will not remove that property alert.

Location Criteria 

  • Here, set the auto alert to only trigger based on the "Inquired City" or "Inquired Zip Code." If you choose "Any," the system will trigger based on city and zip code. 
  • This information is typically gathered when the lead is imported via email parsing and the city or zip code is provided in the email or, if the lead registered on a Lofty website, their activity will be recorded for this purpose.
  • Note: For Canadian clients, the option under "Inquired Zip Code" is intended for Postal Codes; we just don't change the name from "zip code" to "postal codes".

Schedule

  • Due to the large number of emails that are to be sent out, there is no exact time for an alert email. Usually, AM is from 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m., and PM is from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m.

*IMPORTANT: Any Auto Property Alerts that were already created will not be affected by changes to any of these settings.

Reviewing Auto Property Alerts on Leads

On a lead’s profile page, view Auto Property Alerts in the Automations tab. You can edit the settings of Auto Property Alerts to better fit the lead’s criteria, but this turns it into a normal/manual property alert, and this type of alert will not adjust to the lead’s activity (on your website) on its own.

 

Requirements for Auto Alerts

Auto Property Alerts are based on "Search Criteria" and Auto Market Snapshots are based on "Properties".

Note that Auto Property Alerts will only work on leads that meet the following requirements:

Auto Property Alert (Buyer)

  1. The lead has at least one email address
  2. The lead has valid data in the “Location” field of the "Search Criteria" section. If nothing is found in the "Search Criteria" section, an auto property alert email will not be sent until "Location" data is available based on lead behavior on your Lofty IDX website.

Auto Market Snapshot (Seller)

  1. The lead has at least one email address
  2. The lead has data in the “City” or “Zip Code” field of the Detail or Property Info section

Auto Market Report

  1. The lead has at least one email address
  2. If it's a Seller lead. . .
    • The lead has data in the "City" or "Zip Code" fields of a property (Engagement > Properties).
  3. If it's Buyer lead. . .
    • The lead has data for the "City" or "Zip Code" fields in the search criteria (inquiries) on the lead profile.

So, an auto property alert will not be triggered if the information above is not provided or valid. If importing leads that have blank information in these fields, no auto alert will be sent.

 

Frequency of Alert Emails

To improve email deliverability, auto property alert email frequency is adjusted based on the lead's behavior. 

  1. If the lead is set to Instantly get a property alert, and the number of alerts sent in the last 7 days is greater than 6, the alert frequency will adjust to Daily. 
  2. If the lead is set to receive a property alert Daily, and the alert's creation time or last time it was downgraded was more than 7 days, and if at least one alert email has been sent in the last 7 days, then the sending frequency will be set to Weekly.
  3. If the lead is set to receive a property alert Weekly, and the alert creation time or last frequency adjustment time is more than 7 days, and if one alert email has been sent in the last 7 days, then the sending frequency will be adjusted down to Biweekly(every two weeks.)
  4. If the lead is set to receive a property alert Biweekly, the alert creation time or last frequency adjustment time is more than 60 days, and at least one alert email has been sent in the last 7 days, then this will trigger an adjustment down to a Monthly sending frequency.
  5. If the Lead opens an email, the frequency will revert to the original setting, no matter which frequency the system had is moved to due to its previous inactivity. 
    • Example -If the frequency is reduced from instantly > daily > weekly > monthly and then a lead opens an alert type email that they receive then it will go back to instantly.

*Note this applies to Automatic and Manual Property Alerts. 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

body:
Introduction

In the CMS Tool, you can edit the settings associated with the chat box on your website. This is a good way to engage site visitors. 

*IMPORTANT: If the AI Assistant is enabled, the chat box will not appear on your website as the AI Assistant's efforts to engage site visitors take priority.

 

Summary

  • Edit Chat Box Settings
  • Facebook Messenger
  • Live Chat Explanation

 

Edit Chat Box Settings

To edit the chat box, open the CMS Tool > Settings > Lead Capture > Chat Box Settings:

The first setting to edit is whether to display the chat box. Users who choose not to display the chat box might do so to limit the number of available channels on their website to avoid any confusion, or they might want to embed a third-party chat box of some sort (which may require customization and associated customization fees). See below for Facebook Messenger support.
Enabling this setting will display the chat box. Disabling will keep the chat box from appearing on the website at all.

 

Here, you can decide whether to show the Company or the Agent as the Chat Agent. If you choose "Company", the Chat Box leads will be company leads.

 

If you choose "Agent", next select the agent from the available list.

 

Decide whether to display agent information or company information on the chat box.

 

Next, choose the "Agent Image Style," which is simply the shape of the image in the bottom-right:

 

The Chat Bubble Design and Text can also be adjusted. Here, decide whether you want the chat bubble to always appear or only appear when the visitor hovers in the lower right corner.

 

"Main Theme Color" changes will affect the following:

The bubble can also be hidden or set to always display:

The bubble close option can be enabled to allow visitors to close the chat box.

For Chat Mode, the "Live Chat" option will require a text package to use, as it will send messages directly to the Lofty user associated with the Lofty website. "Leave Message" does not require a text package to be used and will simply pop up with a form that the site visitor can complete to leave a message in the system. Their message will trigger an email notification and a push notification to the Lofty user. If you have purchased an AI Assistant, the CMS system will automatically choose the AI Assistant as the Chat Mode.

 

Facebook Messenger

If you turn on the "Facebook Messenger" option, the Lofty chat box will be hidden and instead allow for Facebook Messenger to be used in its place. To work correctly, be sure to set up Facebook Messenger first by following the instructions found here: Install Facebook Messenger.

To finalize the setup, add your Facebook Page ID. Be sure to click "Save," and Facebook Messenger will be installed and ready to use on your Lofty site. 

 

Live Chat Explanation

This section outlines how the "Live Chat" in the Chat Mode setting will actually work.

 

First, a site visitor will click on the chat bubble in the bottom-right of your website:

 

They will be asked to register to communicate with you. They will provide their information and then click on the Register button:

 

After clicking on Register, the questionnaire will appear to them:

 

They would then need to click on the chat box again to send a message. When doing so, they will see a window like the following:

 

The site visitor/lead can send a message via the chat box:

 

Within the CRM, click on the chat bubble in the bottom-right to access website chat conversations:

 

Within the Lofty CRM, you can respond directly within the chat window:

 

That response will be received by the lead in their session on your website:

 

The lead will also receive that message on their cell phone (if compatible) if they provide it during registration.

 

If the lead responds from the website chat box, it will not appear within the text message conversation. For example, the screenshot below shows a response sent by the lead on the website chat box (not via text message). The lead will see any responses from the agent, but not their messages if sent from the web chat box.

 

If the lead messages back via text message (instead of via the website chat box), that message will not appear in the website chat box. In other words, the lead should choose one communication channel and use that.

 

On the agent side, within Lofty, all communication is recorded in the message bubble: 

 

Any messages sent/received via text message (after being initiated via the website chat box) will be synced to the lead profile. If they respond via the website chat box instead, that communication is not recorded on the lead profile.

  

Questions?

title: Feature Updates for CRM 3.0.2, Site 3.6.6
body:
Introduction

*Please note that the features available to you on the Lofty platform will vary depending on the package you have purchased. For any questions in this regard, please reach out to your assigned Customer Success Manager or our Support Team for more information.

Release Date

The release date for this set of features is Monday, November 4, 2019.

Summary

  • Import Reverse Option
  • Add a Lead / Edit a Lead Field Consistency
  • Bounced Email Filter
  • Market Report Timing Optimization
  • Open House Form Creation with MLS Data
  • Opportunity Notification for Additional Form Submissions
  • Transaction Customization

 

Import Reverse Option 

When importing leads, there is often a need to reverse the import and remove the leads that were created because the import was done incorrectly, etc. Lofty now allows users to reverse their import after one has already been processed as long as it is within 24 hours of actually importing the leads. This option is available under Settings > Features > Lead Import > Import History. 

This will work regardless of whether the leads have been contacted, etc. The option will no longer be available after 24 hours of processing the import. The leads will be deleted completely from the system with this option--meaning they will not be sent to the "Deleted Leads" section of the People page.

*For merged leads, they will stay in the system just as imported.

 

Add a Lead / Edit a Lead Field Consistency

Prior to this update, when adding a lead and editing a lead, the options available were different. Now, however, they are the same in both situations in order to stay consistent. 

 

Bounced Email Filter

An additional filter has been added on the People page that now allows Lofty users to filter their leads by those who have had an email address marked as "bounced." If that email is manually marked as "valid" by the Lofty user, it will no longer show up on the filter. This filter only applies to primary email addresses.

The filter option is available under the People page and "Contact Info" on the left side:

 

Market Report Timing Optimization

Lofty has optimized the schedule that a market report is sent out in order to make sure the data is ready before sending out an email with incomplete information. The market report will now be sent out after the data from the prior month is available--typically on the 5th of each month.

 

Open House Form Creation with MLS Data

When creating an Open House form via Lofty, the details and images of that property can now be auto-populated directly from the MLS. The option to manually upload an image is still available.

*This feature is currently only available on the Web App but will also be an option via the Mobile App in an upcoming release.

 

Opportunity Notification for Additional Form Submissions

In addition to the Opportunity notifications mentioned in this Help Center article: Opportunities, Lofty now supports an additional opportunity push and email notification when a current client completes a form on the "Lead Generation" landing page template as well as on the lead form found on neighborhood pages of Templates 1 and 2 (currently not on 3 and 4 because the form disappears for current clients on those templates). 

With each of these, a notification will be triggered like the following:

There will also be a note added on the lead profile indicating where the form was filled out on the website:

 

Transaction Customization

When adding/editing a transaction in Lofty, additional debits/credits can now be recorded per transaction. This is where each of them is recorded:

A summary of this information is also viewable on the Transaction Management page as seen here:

name: Open House Forms
title: Open House Forms
body:
Introduction

The Open House form can be set up on a mobile phone, tablet, or another device that is connected to the internet, to have open house visitors provide their contact information directly on a form that submits it into your CRM. This is the ideal way to capture leads at an open house rather than doing so via a physical pen and paper list as you can set up automation via Lofty Smart Plans to contact these leads immediately or according to a schedule (see Smart Plan Basics).

 

Summary

  • Accessing Open House Forms
  • Create a New Open House Form
  • Open House Questionnaires
  • Manage an Existing Open House Form
  • Using the Open House Form
  • Open Houses and Lead Routing
  • Open Houses and Smart Plans

 

Accessing Open House Forms

Navigate to the Content tab and then click on Open House Forms. Note: you may need permission from your admin to create Open House forms. 

 

Create a New Open House Form

Click the + Add New button to create a new open house. In the "Add Open House" pop-up window, enter the street address, select the questionnaire you want to use, who the Open House Form is shared with, who owns the form, and if the leads who register via the form will receive a welcome email or text and how those leads will be routing to agents on your team.

Each Open House Form is created for a specific listing, but the questionnaires can be used on multiple open house forms. 

Open House Questionnaires

The Open House Questionnaire provides the details that are collected from leads at your open house. To get started, click Questionnaires, then click + Add New. 

The questionnaire has some default fields for the leads' name, email address, and phone number, along with the option to make the field required. If required, they cannot finish the form without completing all required fields. The form is completely customizable and you can add, remove, or re-order all of the form fields. 

Learn how to navigate the Questionnaire:

  1. Scope: Select who this questionnaire is available to. This could be private for your own use or available to anyone in your team, office, or company.
  2. Add a Question: Add a new plain text or multiple choice question to the questionnaire.
  3. Questionnaire Name: This questionnaire will be saved as a template that can be used on multiple Open House Forms, so give it a recognizable name.
  4. Required vs. Optional: If the box next to the question is checked, the field must be complete for the lead to complete the questionnaire.
  5. Hamburger Menu: Click this icon to re-order the questionnaire questions. Click the icon and drag the question to its new placement.
  6. Trash Can: Click this icon to delete the question.
  7. Do Not Enter: Click this icon to delete a multiple choice option.
  8. Add a Choice: Add a new multiple choice option here. 

Once your questionnaire is complete, click Save and you can view the questionnaire in the list of other questionnaire templates. Under Actions, you have the option to edit or delete an existing Open House Questionnaire template.



 

Manage an Existing Open House Form

To edit or delete an Open House Form, hover on the selected form and click either the edit or trash can icon.

 

Using the Open House Form

To use the form, first log in to your Lofty account via a computer, tablet, or the Lofty mobile app. Note that there is no app for iPad or Android tablets but you can open Lofty via a mobile browser, sign in, and access the form. Navigate to your Open House page and select the form for the Open House. 

From here, leads can scan the QR code to complete the form on their phone or they can fill in the form directly on the computer you provide. You can also print out the QR code for leads to scan on their own. 

Once leads click the Submit button to send the form. They will immediately be registered into the Lofty CRM.

On the submission page of the questionnaire, you can add a Visitor Note or choose to let the next visitor continue the sign-in.

The leads that register will have the source of "Open House" and a shared tag of the address for the listing (not city/state/zip). This will help you to easily find these clients later on.

The answers to the questionnaire are added to the lead profile. Those that match up with standard fields supported in Lofty will be added to the applicable field. Those include the following:

  • Multiple Choice (With Agent) --> With Agent
     
  • Multiple Choice (Price) --> Search Criteria- Price
     
  • Multiple Choice (House to sell) --> House to Sell
     
  • Multiple Choice (TimeFrame) --> Time Frame
     
  • Multiple Choice (Pre-qual) --> Pre-qualified
     
  • Multiple Choice (FTHB) --> First-Time Buyer

Any customized questions that are asked in the questionnaire will be added to the lead profile as a note.

 

Open Houses and Lead Routing

If you want to route the incoming leads from the open house to others on your team, be sure to check the box next to Assign lead by routing?. This box is not checked, by default.

 

Next, navigate to Settings > Lead Routing and make sure you have a lead routing rule set up to capture and route these leads appropriately. Learn more about lead routing here: Lead Routing Rules

Open Houses and Smart Plans

Since you have just met the lead at the Open House, you may want to put them on a Smart Plan to stay in touch. Learn more about Smart Plans here: Managing Smart Plans

A quick tip is to set up a Smart Plan trigger for when a new lead is created from the Open House source. This will ensure that any new leads from the open house will automatically be subscribed to your selected Smart Plan. 

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat with us through your Lofty CRM.

name: Voice Messages for Inbound & Outbound Calls
title: Voice Messages for Inbound & Outbound Calls
body:
Introduction

It can be frustrating to call leads when they go straight to voicemail. Recording a new message every time is not only tedious but also time-consuming. Lofty can help you save time by allowing you to pre-record voice messages for more effective use of your time. 

 

To access these options, navigate to Settings > Communication > Call & Text > Voice Messages.

 

Record an Outbound Call Voice Message

*This feature is included in all Lofty call packages.

To add a new Outbound Call Voice Message, click on the "Add" button:

 

You can record five messages within the Outbound Call Voice Message category.

To record the message, you will need to enter your phone number. You will then receive a call with step-by-step instructions to record the message.

Give the voice message a name and then click on the blue "Save" button. The name can always be adjusted later.

 

 

 

 

Use the Outbound Call Voice Messages

For outbound calls, you can leave a recorded voicemail instead of recording a new one every time.  After dropping your voice message, the call will disconnect automatically.

Make sure to drop your voice message only after the answering system triggers the "beep."

 

 

After selecting the Voice Message option, the names of the recordings you have made will appear for you to choose from.

 

 

 

Record an Inbound Call Voice Message

*This feature is included in all Lofty call packages.

A default always needs to be selected by clicking the toggle to the on position. You can record up to five voice messages to be available for inbound calls.

 

To record a new message, click on the "Add" button:

 

To record the message, you will need to enter your phone number, and then you will receive a call with step-by-step instructions to record the message.

Give the voice message a name and then click on the blue "Save" button. The name can always be adjusted later.

 

 

 

 

Use the Inbound Call Voice Messages

*This feature is included in all Lofty call packages.

When you are unavailable to answer inbound calls, your leads will be directed to your pre-recorded voice message.

Inbound callers will only be directed to Lofty's inbound call voice message if you are not available (if you are not within working/available hours of what you configured on their Lofty account.) If you are available for calls in Lofty, the inbound call will still be bridged to your bridge number reason why your caller will hear the voicemail of your mobile phone (bridge number).

See this article for more information about setting your availability: Availability (Working Hours) for Phone Calls.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please get in touch with our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com>, by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557, or by chat through your CRM.

body:
Introduction

*Please note that the features available to you on the Lofty platform will vary depending on the package you have purchased. For any questions in this regard, please reach out to your assigned Customer Success Manager or our Support Team for more information.

Release Date

The release date for this set of features is Monday, October 21, 2019.

Summary

  • Slybroadcast Integration (Web)
  • Undelivered Texts on Lead Profile Timelines (Web & App)
  • Landing Page Tag/Note Optimization (Web)
  • Smart Plan Optimizations (4) (Web)
  • MLS Agent ID Search (Web)
  • Direct Mail Text Code Feature (Print Product Only)

 

Slybroadcast Integration

Lofty now integrates directly with Slybroadcast! With this feature, users can send pre-recorded voice messages to leads individually, in batches, or via scheduled Smart Plans ("My Smart Plans" only). Voice messages that are sent will be documented in lead profile timelines.

Specific information on how this integration works can be found HERE.

To subscribe to Slybroadcast, click HERE.

 

Undelivered Texts on Lead Profile Timelines

The delivery status of texts sent via Lofty will now be documented on each lead profile. Here is how it displays:

Also, a new filter is available on the People Page that can be used to search for leads where messages have failed to deliver so that an email or phone call can be completed instead:

 

Landing Page Tag/Note Optimization

When building landing pages via the CMS Tool, the "Lead Generation" template also provides settings to add a note and/or a tag to leads that register via that landing page:

With this update, this feature has been optimized so that tags and notes can also be added to existing leads already in the database if they complete the form again.

 

Smart Plan Optimizations (4)

(1) Excluding current leads in the database 

Previous to this update, whenever "Auto Apply" conditions are set up on a Smart Plan, all current leads and new leads will BOTH be added to that Smart Plan as long as they match the criteria. With this update, however, the criteria for “whenever leads meet the specified conditions” will now have the following options to select from:

  • include current applicable leads
  • exclude current applicable leads

With the second option, all current leads that match the specified conditions can be skipped on this Smart Plan for situations when you have already been working those leads and do not want to start them on a new Smart Plan.

*Should you want to exclude more leads, the criteria can always be edited.

(2) Send first auto email/text during a specific time range

This option is available for "Immediately" and "Wait ___ hour(s), ___ minute(s)." When selected, if the Smart Plan is triggered before the indicated time range, the auto email/text will be sent at the first available time within that range. If triggered after the indicated range, the auto email/text will be sent the following day at the first available time within the range.

(3) Resubscribe leads to Smart Plans if lead has accidentally unsubscribed

To resubscribe for the lead, go to Lead Profile > Smart Plans > Click on the gear icon at the top right. This switch was previously locked. Now, it can be turned back on to resubscribe the lead to Smart Plans.

(4) New auto email Lead Variables

Lofty has added two new lead variables to reference buyer-related property addresses in Smart Plan auto emails and auto texts. The new variables are the following:

  • buyer_inquired_listing_addr. The address of the property that is associated with the lead's initial inquiry.
  • trigger_behavior_listing_addr. The address of the related listing when the Smart Plan is triggered by leads requesting showings, saving listings, or viewing a listing multiple times.

Lead Variables can be found here when building an email template directly in a Smart Plan:

 

MLS Agent ID Search

Lofty users can now find their "MLS Agent ID" by searching by listing address or MLS Listing ID. To do this, simply click on the "Need Help?" hyperlink under Settings > User > Profile > to the right of MLS Agent ID.  As a reminder, the MLS Agent ID is a requirement for certain features to work including certain Listing Discovery and Transaction Management features as it helps Lofty locate your MLS listings or your MLS transactions.

 

Direct Mail Text Code Feature (Print Product Only)

A brand new text code feature will be available for clients who have purchased Lofty's Direct Mail (or Print) product. For each client, Lofty assigns a virtual number and a unique code for each and every postcard that is sent out for geo farming. When homeowners text the text code to the number on the postcards, they will get a home evaluation report immediately. Meanwhile Lofty tracks and imports the homeowners’ info into the CRM.

When homeowners call the number on the postcard, Lofty will display the lead source on the phone and track and log inbound calls on the CRM.

 

Questions?

If you have any questions regarding this topic or any others, please reach out to our Support Team via email at <support@lofty.com> or by phone at 1 (855) 981-7557.

name: How To Add a Property Address Under Lead's Preferences

body:
Introduction

Adding a property address to a Lead Profile can help you know their preference better and keep track of the properties that they are associated with. Listings that have been saved by a lead on the Lofty IDX website will also show up in this section.

 

Add a Property Manually

First, choose a lead on the “People” page:

Click the Properties tab.

 

Click “+” to add a property. Add any additional details that you might know about the property.

 

Input the property address. Please note that this field is required. You can select an address from the drop-down box or record the Unit or the PO Box of this property in the “Unit/PO Box” field.

*Note: If you want to input a Canada address, please ensure your browser language settings have been changed to English (Canada). Using Chrome, for example, Settings > Advanced > Language > Language > English (Canada) > Move to the top.

 Choose the label from the options available that best describes this property:

  • Selling: 
    • Home (Default)
    • Investment
    • Lease
    • Listed
    • Sold
  • Buying: 
    • High Interest
    • Saved Listing
    • Left Message
    • Requested Showing
    • Finished Showing
    • Under Contract
    • Purchased

Please note that if leads have corresponding activity on the website, a property will be created automatically and labeled as “Saved Listing / Left Message / Requested Showing...” This property would also be removed automatically if the lead goes back and removes that listing from their saved listings.

Fill in the basic info about this property. Such as beds, baths, price, etc. When you fill in all the information, just click the “Save” button.

 

Use a Property

The main purpose of the property section is to have a place where properties can be saved. An image of the property can be previewed, and the following actions can be taken as well:

1. Send a CMA Report / Listing Presentation

Lofty does not create CMA reports but does integrate with CloudCMA. The only reason "Send CMA" will work is if this needs to be integrated with Cloud CMA first. More information can be found here: How to Integrate Cloud CMA with Your Lofty CRM.

 

2. Create a Transaction

Create a transaction based on this property. More information regarding how to use transactions can be found here: Transaction Management.

 

3. Send Home Report

Email your lead with this home report. Only available when this property is listed on the MLS.

 

 

Questions?
